<i>So option one then is</i>
<i>Michele and Tony go to fire.</i>

1813
01:25:01,179 --> 01:25:04,182
For me, my goal is to be able
to make Tony look

1814
01:25:04,265 --> 01:25:07,352
as less desirable as a winner
as possible.

1815
01:25:07,435 --> 01:25:08,353
Obviously, you don't want
to go to fire,

1816
01:25:08,436 --> 01:25:11,397
but if Sarah wins,

1817
01:25:11,481 --> 01:25:13,358
that gives her cred
to beat me in the end.

1818
01:25:13,441 --> 01:25:15,026
<i>MICHELE:</i>
<i>I would love</i>

1819
01:25:15,109 --> 01:25:16,861
to win the fire-making
challenge.

1820
01:25:16,945 --> 01:25:19,697
<i>It's a really good endcap.</i>

1821
01:25:19,781 --> 01:25:21,616
It's just a really risky way
to end the game.

1822
01:25:24,244 --> 01:25:27,914
<i>But it's times like this</i>
<i>when, honestly,</i>

1823
01:25:27,997 --> 01:25:29,624
my strengths have come out.

1824
01:25:36,130 --> 01:25:37,549
<i>TONY:</i>
<i>So I was watching Michele.</i>

1825
01:25:37,632 --> 01:25:38,883
<i>She's striking it.</i>

1826
01:25:38,967 --> 01:25:40,552
She's like...
(imitates clicking) Flame.

1827
01:25:40,635 --> 01:25:43,930
<i>So I'm a little concerned</i>
<i>about that.</i>

1828
01:25:44,013 --> 01:25:45,431
Doing it quicker than that?

1829
01:25:45,515 --> 01:25:46,891
-Yeah.
-How are you doing it?

1830
01:25:46,975 --> 01:25:50,061
I'm not telling you,
just in case we go up together.

1831
01:25:50,144 --> 01:25:51,563
Good job, Mich.

1832
01:25:51,646 --> 01:25:53,356
-How's Michele doing up there?
-She's doing good.

1833
01:25:53,439 --> 01:25:54,440
-Oh, she is?
-Yeah.

1834
01:25:54,524 --> 01:25:56,067
-She making fire?
-Yeah.

1835
01:25:56,150 --> 01:25:56,985
-She is?
-Yeah.

1836
01:25:57,777 --> 01:25:59,571
<i>TONY:</i>
<i>I literally sat there</i>

1837
01:25:59,654 --> 01:26:01,781
<i>and watched Michele</i>
<i>scrape it once or twice,</i>

1838
01:26:01,865 --> 01:26:03,908
the magnesium, and she was good.

1839
01:26:03,992 --> 01:26:06,452
-Damn, I need to get good
at this, man.
-I know, T.

1840
01:26:08,496 --> 01:26:10,957
<i>SARAH: We're just grinding</i>
<i>all afternoon,</i>

1841
01:26:11,040 --> 01:26:13,376
because you have no choice
but to grind at this point.

1842
01:26:13,459 --> 01:26:16,588
<i>I hope she picks me.</i>

1843
01:26:16,671 --> 01:26:17,922
<i>I want to step up to the plate.</i>

1844
01:26:18,006 --> 01:26:19,549
I'm not scared. Pick me.

1845
01:26:19,632 --> 01:26:22,051
Wow. Now I'm panicking, man.

1846
01:26:22,135 --> 01:26:23,136
<i>SARAH:</i>
<i>Tony's not in</i>

1847
01:26:23,219 --> 01:26:23,428
the right headspace
to make fire.

1848
01:26:26,014 --> 01:26:30,268
<i>Maybe he can get there,</i>
<i>but if he doesn't get there,</i>

1849
01:26:30,351 --> 01:26:31,728
I'm gonna beat him in fire.

1850
01:26:31,811 --> 01:26:34,731
<i>TONY:</i>
<i>I wish I could have</i>
<i>the easy route,</i>

1851
01:26:34,814 --> 01:26:36,065
but I always take
the hard route.

1852
01:26:37,650 --> 01:26:39,110
(sighs):
Ah, man.

1853
01:26:39,193 --> 01:26:40,028
That's what I do, man.
I grind.

1854
01:26:40,111 --> 01:26:42,614
<i>I work hard,</i>
<i>I'm gonna practice hard,</i>

1855
01:26:42,697 --> 01:26:43,948
<i>I'm gonna try to perform hard.</i>

1856
01:26:44,032 --> 01:26:45,450
<i>Tonight's gonna be</i>
<i>put up or shut up.</i>

1857
01:26:45,533 --> 01:26:47,952
Fire!

1858
01:26:48,036 --> 01:26:50,830
I'm either gonna win this game
or I'm gonna lose trying.

1859
01:26:50,914 --> 01:26:52,957
It all boils down to this.

1860
01:26:54,542 --> 01:26:56,544
♪ ♪

1861
01:27:00,840 --> 01:27:03,635
<i>NATALIE:</i>
<i>Tonight, I'm sitting</i>
<i>in the front seat,</i>

1862
01:27:03,718 --> 01:27:05,803
<i>after being in the back seat</i>
<i>all this time,</i>

1863
01:27:05,887 --> 01:27:06,471
<i>getting voted off first.</i>

1864
01:27:10,600 --> 01:27:12,810
<i>I would rather be</i>
<i>in this position</i>

1865
01:27:12,894 --> 01:27:15,063
<i>than having</i>
<i>somebody else dictate</i>

1866
01:27:15,146 --> 01:27:18,149
<i>what's gonna happen</i>
<i>with my fate on the game.</i>

1867
01:27:18,232 --> 01:27:19,984
<i>I have all the power</i>

1868
01:27:20,068 --> 01:27:23,154
<i>and the biggest and last</i>
<i>decision of the game.</i>

1869
01:27:23,237 --> 01:27:25,156
Now bring in the members
of our jury.

1870
01:27:32,121 --> 01:27:35,083
All right, so let's get into it.

1871
01:27:35,166 --> 01:27:37,043
Sophie is not with us tonight.

1872
01:27:37,126 --> 01:27:39,003
Sophie's not feeling well,

1873
01:27:39,087 --> 01:27:41,381
so she can't attend
tonight's Tribal,

1874
01:27:41,464 --> 01:27:43,841
-but you guys will
fill her in...
-Yeah, for sure.

1875
01:27:43,925 --> 01:27:46,052
...in as unbiased a way
as possible.

1876
01:27:46,135 --> 01:27:47,679
-Of course.
-All right.

1877
01:27:47,762 --> 01:27:52,016
Natalie, the final immunity
challenge, you pull it out.

1878
01:27:52,100 --> 01:27:55,311
Go back to that moment,
when you think about day two,

1879
01:27:55,395 --> 01:27:57,522
you're the first person sent
to the Edge of Extinction,

1880
01:27:57,605 --> 01:28:00,316
all alone,

1881
01:28:00,400 --> 01:28:03,152
to this moment, where you are
in the final three,

1882
01:28:03,236 --> 01:28:05,154
one of the most
improbable things

1883
01:28:05,238 --> 01:28:06,531
that you could ever imagine
on<i> Survivor.</i>

1884
01:28:06,614 --> 01:28:08,700
NATALIE:
It's crazy.

1885
01:28:08,783 --> 01:28:11,160
Felt like a dream, but I think
it was the only thing

1886
01:28:11,244 --> 01:28:14,831
that kept me going at Extinction
was telling myself

1887
01:28:14,914 --> 01:28:17,458
that I would get this shot
to battle back,

1888
01:28:17,542 --> 01:28:20,545
and then you putting
this necklace on me was

1889
01:28:20,628 --> 01:28:23,381
the most amazing feeling
I've had so far.

1890
01:28:23,464 --> 01:28:24,424
Hard work pays off.

1891
01:28:24,507 --> 01:28:27,552
So, Michele, what was
the afternoon like?

1892
01:28:27,635 --> 01:28:31,723
I'm guessing everybody wanted
a chance to talk to Natalie.

1893
01:28:31,806 --> 01:28:34,267
Well, Natalie actually
came back to camp

1894
01:28:34,350 --> 01:28:37,103
and said that she should
allow us to converse

1895
01:28:37,186 --> 01:28:41,399
and she wanted some time alone
to contemplate her decision.

1896
01:28:41,482 --> 01:28:45,653
And since then, I didn't eat,
I didn't take a sip of my water.

1897
01:28:45,737 --> 01:28:49,365
I practiced fire
from the moment that I got back.

1898
01:28:49,449 --> 01:28:51,242
PROBST:
Tony, do you spend much time

1899
01:28:51,326 --> 01:28:54,203
thinking about who you want
to go up against

1900
01:28:54,287 --> 01:28:55,121
or do you spend
more time thinking,

1901
01:28:55,204 --> 01:28:57,874
"I just need to be the best,
that's it"?

1902
01:28:57,957 --> 01:29:00,251
I just come here and give it
my best. That's all I do.

1903
01:29:00,335 --> 01:29:02,086
I play as hard as I can,
uh, nonstop,

1904
01:29:02,170 --> 01:29:05,089
hoping that my best is
good enough to win in the end.

1905
01:29:05,173 --> 01:29:07,216
So you don't care
who you go up against in fire?

1906
01:29:07,300 --> 01:29:08,926
-Right now? No.
-How about you, Sarah?

1907
01:29:09,010 --> 01:29:10,303
Do you have a preference?

1908
01:29:10,386 --> 01:29:11,220
SARAH:
If I'm making fire,

1909
01:29:11,304 --> 01:29:13,097
it's gonna be against Tony.

1910
01:29:13,181 --> 01:29:14,599
And I don't think

1911
01:29:14,682 --> 01:29:17,268
I would truly want to make fire
against anyone else.

1912
01:29:17,351 --> 01:29:18,436
Why?

1913
01:29:18,519 --> 01:29:21,314
(voice breaking):
I mean, I love this guy and...

1914
01:29:21,397 --> 01:29:21,981
Oh. Stop, stop, man.

1915
01:29:22,065 --> 01:29:24,358
-Relax.
-He's my partner.

1916
01:29:24,442 --> 01:29:25,902
And, uh...

1917
01:29:25,985 --> 01:29:29,447
if we're gonna get shot,
I'd rather us shoot each other

1918
01:29:29,530 --> 01:29:32,116
than have someone else
shoot at us, so...

1919
01:29:32,200 --> 01:29:33,534
Wait, you want to shoot me now?

1920
01:29:33,618 --> 01:29:35,912
-Yeah.
-(Tony chuckles)

1921
01:29:35,995 --> 01:29:37,747
PROBST:
How about you, Michele?

1922
01:29:37,830 --> 01:29:39,123
Is there a preference?

1923
01:29:39,207 --> 01:29:41,626
If I had to make fire, I would
want to make it against Tony,

1924
01:29:41,709 --> 01:29:44,295
because I think that he stands

1925
01:29:44,378 --> 01:29:46,297
the best shot of
winning this game right now.

1926
01:29:46,380 --> 01:29:49,634
And, Natalie,
that's the dilemma you have is:

1927
01:29:49,717 --> 01:29:54,055
Do you put yourself in that spot
and say, "I'm gonna just do it,"

1928
01:29:54,138 --> 01:29:57,016
or, "Whose the best person
to try to get rid of

1929
01:29:57,100 --> 01:29:58,684
who I think might be
my biggest target?"

1930
01:29:58,768 --> 01:29:59,727
NATALIE:
Exactly.

1931
01:29:59,811 --> 01:30:01,437
And I would love to battle Tony,

1932
01:30:01,521 --> 01:30:04,398
send him home
and sit here tomorrow...

1933
01:30:04,482 --> 01:30:05,483
Well, what's stopping you?

1934
01:30:05,566 --> 01:30:08,152
Um, be-- I have to be
brutally honest with myself

1935
01:30:08,236 --> 01:30:11,781
and ask myself, "Do I feel
100% confidence in beating him?"

1936
01:30:11,864 --> 01:30:14,200
At this point, I feel like,
when I won the challenge today

1937
01:30:14,283 --> 01:30:16,661
and you put this immunity
necklace around my neck,

1938
01:30:16,744 --> 01:30:20,373
I knew that I had done enough
and felt satisfied

1939
01:30:20,456 --> 01:30:22,458
to leave the fire-making
to somebody else tonight.

1940
01:30:22,542 --> 01:30:25,169
PROBST:
All right, so let's get to it,
Natalie.

1941
01:30:25,253 --> 01:30:27,213
You have one decision to make.

1942
01:30:27,296 --> 01:30:29,173
Who are you going to bring
with you to the end?

1943
01:30:29,257 --> 01:30:31,676
And the two you leave behind
will move right over here

1944
01:30:31,759 --> 01:30:33,678
and showdown in fire.

1945
01:30:33,761 --> 01:30:36,556
The person I'm bringing
with me tonight

1946
01:30:36,639 --> 01:30:38,224
is gonna be Michele.

1947
01:30:38,307 --> 01:30:41,644
She's gonna be sitting
at the final three with me.

1948
01:30:41,727 --> 01:30:43,396
-Surprise, surprise.
-Like I said,

1949
01:30:43,479 --> 01:30:44,647
until last minute, it wasn't.

1950
01:30:44,730 --> 01:30:48,109
But I want to see
the end of this alliance.

1951
01:30:48,192 --> 01:30:49,068
I think that Michele and I

1952
01:30:49,152 --> 01:30:51,571
worked the last couple of days
really hard.

1953
01:30:51,654 --> 01:30:54,866
-And we took apart
the foursome...
-(coughing)

1954
01:30:54,949 --> 01:30:56,200
-...one by one.
-Sorry.

1955
01:30:56,284 --> 01:30:58,536
-And this'll be
the last showdown.
-(Sarah coughing)

1956
01:30:58,619 --> 01:31:02,331
And I'm hoping that this girl
is sitting with me at the end.

1957
01:31:02,415 --> 01:31:03,833
PROBST:
So let's set the stage.

1958
01:31:03,916 --> 01:31:05,710
Natalie, you're in
the final three.

1959
01:31:05,793 --> 01:31:07,336
-Yeah.
-You are bringing
Michele with you.

1960
01:31:07,420 --> 01:31:10,256
You are going to force
Sarah and Tony

1961
01:31:10,339 --> 01:31:14,469
to battle it out for that final
spot in a fire-making showdown.

1962
01:31:14,552 --> 01:31:16,220
Tony, you'll take
this spot in red.

1963
01:31:16,304 --> 01:31:18,347
Sarah will take blue.

1964
01:31:19,515 --> 01:31:21,309
♪ ♪

1965
01:31:41,329 --> 01:31:42,914
-All right, Tony, Sarah,
are you ready?
-Yeah.

1966
01:31:42,997 --> 01:31:43,915
Good luck.

1967
01:31:43,998 --> 01:31:47,251
This could be a $2 million fire.

1968
01:31:47,501 --> 01:31:49,754
Finally gonna have to say
I'm better than you.

1969
01:31:50,671 --> 01:31:52,715
Yeah, it's all right.

1970
01:31:54,884 --> 01:31:58,137
Here we go. Begin.

1971
01:32:00,514 --> 01:32:02,600
You both have the same supplies.

1972
01:32:03,684 --> 01:32:07,521
What you do with them
is what matters.

1973
01:32:08,689 --> 01:32:11,609
Out of the gate,
two different approaches.

1974
01:32:11,692 --> 01:32:14,070
Tony scraping magnesium.

1975
01:32:14,153 --> 01:32:17,073
Sarah building a little nest.

1976
01:32:18,366 --> 01:32:20,493
PROBST:
Tony going for a spark.

1977
01:32:22,536 --> 01:32:25,248
A little flame.
Got to get it to take.

1978
01:32:25,331 --> 01:32:27,625
He's got magnesium in that husk.

1979
01:32:27,708 --> 01:32:30,795
Trying to get it to catch.
Sarah now scraping magnesium.

1980
01:32:32,755 --> 01:32:35,132
Sarah has a little bit of flame.

1981
01:32:35,216 --> 01:32:36,717
It goes out.

1982
01:32:45,726 --> 01:32:49,188
Tony has a little bit of flame.
Can he keep it going?

1983
01:32:50,773 --> 01:32:51,983
(blowing)

1984
01:32:52,066 --> 01:32:54,819
Key is, once you get it,
to nurture it

1985
01:32:54,902 --> 01:32:56,946
so it doesn't go out.

1986
01:32:57,905 --> 01:33:00,574
Tony's trying to keep his going.

1987
01:33:00,658 --> 01:33:01,742
Blowing ever so gently.

1988
01:33:05,871 --> 01:33:09,500
Sarah not panicking.

1989
01:33:09,583 --> 01:33:11,669
Sarah has another baby flame.

1990
01:33:13,254 --> 01:33:14,839
Yep. Yep. Yep.

1991
01:33:16,841 --> 01:33:19,510
Sarah's flame is going now.

1992
01:33:19,594 --> 01:33:20,553
Tony's is going.

1993
01:33:20,636 --> 01:33:20,970
Sarah's trying
to keep hers going.

1994
01:33:21,053 --> 01:33:22,805
Oh, my God.

1995
01:33:25,308 --> 01:33:29,020
PROBST: Both very close with
about the same amount of flame.

1996
01:33:30,938 --> 01:33:34,275
Now it's gonna come down to
who can build a fire

1997
01:33:34,358 --> 01:33:35,818
high enough
to burn through that rope.

1998
01:33:37,820 --> 01:33:40,740
Both doing a nice job.

1999
01:33:40,823 --> 01:33:42,742
You only have so much husk,

2000
01:33:42,825 --> 01:33:46,037
which is why it's so critical
when you use it.

2001
01:33:46,120 --> 01:33:48,748
Sarah's flame is now
in the lead.

2002
01:33:52,585 --> 01:33:54,795
Sarah's using
all of her coconut husk.

2003
01:33:54,879 --> 01:33:55,755
Oh. Oh.

2004
01:33:55,838 --> 01:33:57,757
PROBST:
Trying to burn
through that rope.

2005
01:33:57,840 --> 01:34:00,259
Oh, ....

2006
01:34:00,343 --> 01:34:03,721
PROBST: Tony's flame
starting to diminish.

2007
01:34:10,978 --> 01:34:14,607
Now Sarah's is back
diminishing again.

2008
01:34:18,694 --> 01:34:19,737
Add some sticks.

2009
01:34:24,116 --> 01:34:27,620
PROBST: Tony building
a giant structure for a bonfire.

2010
01:34:27,703 --> 01:34:29,580
(quiet murmuring)

2011
01:34:29,663 --> 01:34:31,248
All that matters is
burning through that rope,

2012
01:34:31,332 --> 01:34:32,750
and now it's Tony
back in the lead.

2013
01:34:32,833 --> 01:34:34,377
This has been back and forth,

2014
01:34:34,460 --> 01:34:38,089
-one of the best fire-making
challenges we have ever had.
-(others murmuring)

2015
01:34:41,509 --> 01:34:43,511
PROBST:
Sarah's flame is back now.

2016
01:34:45,846 --> 01:34:47,223
Wow.

2017
01:34:47,306 --> 01:34:48,974
PROBST:
Tony's flame is burning strong.

2018
01:34:49,058 --> 01:34:51,685
It's starting to burn
through that rope now.

2019
01:34:54,146 --> 01:34:55,940
PROBST: Sarah's flame
burning very strong,

2020
01:34:56,023 --> 01:34:58,234
starting to burn
through that rope.

2021
01:34:59,276 --> 01:35:01,946
Tony's flame is
really strong right now.

2022
01:35:02,029 --> 01:35:04,698
It is a showdown.

2023
01:35:11,705 --> 01:35:14,417
-Yeah!
-(whooping)
-PROBST: And it is over.

2024
01:35:14,500 --> 01:35:15,835
Tony defeats Sarah.

2025
01:35:15,918 --> 01:35:18,838
He'll take the third
and final spot

2026
01:35:18,921 --> 01:35:21,424
at the final Tribal Council.

2027
01:35:21,507 --> 01:35:24,468
What a showdown
between competitors.

2028
01:35:30,433 --> 01:35:32,476
Cops-R-Us.

2029
01:35:32,560 --> 01:35:32,893
SARAH:
Oh, my God, you won.

2030
01:35:32,977 --> 01:35:33,936
I love you.

2031
01:35:35,020 --> 01:35:37,273
Hey. Hey.

2032
01:35:37,356 --> 01:35:38,983
Hey. We did-- Hey.

2033
01:35:39,066 --> 01:35:40,985
-You don't have to be sorry
for anything.
-Sorry.

2034
01:35:41,068 --> 01:35:42,820
-Hey, listen.
-I got you. I know.

2035
01:35:42,903 --> 01:35:44,822
I want you to enjoy
that breakfast tomorrow.

2036
01:35:44,905 --> 01:35:46,031
-All right?
-Yeah.

2037
01:35:46,115 --> 01:35:47,491
Hey. Hey.

2038
01:35:47,575 --> 01:35:48,701
Enjoy this.

2039
01:35:48,784 --> 01:35:50,911
-You got one more day
and you're done.
-Shh. Shh.

2040
01:35:50,995 --> 01:35:51,996
One more.

2041
01:35:52,079 --> 01:35:52,872
TONY:
I'm so sorry, man.

2042
01:35:52,955 --> 01:35:54,832
SARAH:
Don't apologize to me.

2043
01:35:54,915 --> 01:35:57,793
I'm not going
to say sorry for it.

2044
01:36:00,796 --> 01:36:02,715
-I love you.
-I love you.

2045
01:36:02,798 --> 01:36:04,550
Thanks.

2046
01:36:07,928 --> 01:36:11,724
PROBST:
So, Sarah, how does
that feel right now

2047
01:36:11,807 --> 01:36:13,768
knowing that the quest
for the two million

2048
01:36:13,851 --> 01:36:17,688
and the title is over,
by a few sticks?

2049
01:36:17,771 --> 01:36:18,439
SARAH:
(sighs) Um...

2050
01:36:18,522 --> 01:36:20,900
(clears throat)
I mean, it's...

2051
01:36:20,983 --> 01:36:21,901
it's okay.

2052
01:36:21,984 --> 01:36:26,655
And when you hear
people say that,

2053
01:36:26,739 --> 01:36:27,072
it doesn't mean
they're giving up.

2054
01:36:27,156 --> 01:36:28,908
It means that...

2055
01:36:28,991 --> 01:36:31,911
they got something valuable
out of this experience.

2056
01:36:31,994 --> 01:36:36,207
And (sniffles) if I was
gonna go out of this game,

2057
01:36:36,290 --> 01:36:37,708
that's how I wanted to go out.

2058
01:36:37,791 --> 01:36:40,711
And if I wanted someone
to take me out,

2059
01:36:40,794 --> 01:36:41,629
that's who I wanted
to take me out.

2060
01:36:41,712 --> 01:36:44,757
And if someone was
gonna take him out,

2061
01:36:44,840 --> 01:36:46,050
I wanted it to be me.

2062
01:36:46,133 --> 01:36:49,345
And, um...

2063
01:36:49,428 --> 01:36:52,765
Tony is more than deserving to
be sitting in the final three,

2064
01:36:52,848 --> 01:36:56,727
and... I wish I could
be there with him.

2065
01:36:56,810 --> 01:36:57,686
You know?

2066
01:36:57,770 --> 01:37:00,564
We talked about this
for the last 38 days.

2067
01:37:00,648 --> 01:37:03,400
Um, it's not gonna happen,
but it's okay.

2068
01:37:03,484 --> 01:37:07,071
And he can still finish
what he set out to accomplish,

2069
01:37:07,154 --> 01:37:10,908
and I know he's gonna do it,
and so I'm fine.

2070
01:37:10,991 --> 01:37:16,580
PROBST:
All right, Sarah,
this season is over for you.

2071
01:37:16,664 --> 01:37:18,290
Need to bring me your torch.

2072
01:37:18,374 --> 01:37:20,668
♪ ♪

2073
01:37:27,007 --> 01:37:29,718
Lacina, the tribe has spoken.

2074
01:37:31,679 --> 01:37:32,930
-Time for you to go.
-Thanks.

2075
01:37:33,013 --> 01:37:34,598
It was a pleasure.

2076
01:37:34,682 --> 01:37:35,724
Tony...

2077
01:37:35,808 --> 01:37:37,810
-(sniffles)
-I love you.

2078
01:37:37,893 --> 01:37:39,812
Crush it tomorrow, all right?

2079
01:37:39,895 --> 01:37:40,813
Eat some food for me.

2080
01:37:40,896 --> 01:37:43,315
I'll be eating it
for you tonight.

2081
01:37:43,399 --> 01:37:44,942
(howls)

2082
01:37:46,026 --> 01:37:46,944
(sniffles)

2083
01:37:51,073 --> 01:37:53,576
PROBST:
Okay.

2084
01:37:53,659 --> 01:37:55,744
Natalie, Tony, Michele.

2085
01:37:55,828 --> 01:37:58,163
You had three different journeys
to get here, but you did it.

2086
01:37:58,247 --> 01:38:01,041
You made it to the final three
of our 40th season.

2087
01:38:01,125 --> 01:38:04,795
Tomorrow night,
you will face the jury,

2088
01:38:04,878 --> 01:38:06,755
people you voted out
of this game,

2089
01:38:06,839 --> 01:38:09,508
people who understand what
it takes to get to this spot.

2090
01:38:09,592 --> 01:38:11,760
They're gonna have
a lot of questions.

2091
01:38:11,844 --> 01:38:14,138
Tomorrow, somebody,
one of the three of you,

2092
01:38:14,221 --> 01:38:17,975
is gonna show up and seize
the title of Sole Survivor

2093
01:38:18,058 --> 01:38:20,644
and the $2 million prize.

2094
01:38:20,728 --> 01:38:23,480
One last night of sleep in Fiji.

2095
01:38:23,564 --> 01:38:25,983
Try to make it a good one.
See you tomorrow.

2096
01:38:26,066 --> 01:38:26,984
Grab your torches,
head back to camp.

2097
01:38:27,067 --> 01:38:28,027
Good night.

2098
01:38:28,110 --> 01:38:30,988
Tony's my partner in crime
for life.

2099
01:38:31,071 --> 01:38:33,032
<i>If I'm gonna have to end</i>
<i>my</i> Survivor<i> career,</i>

2100
01:38:33,115 --> 01:38:37,286
<i>how else would I want to end it</i>
<i>than like this?</i>

2101
01:38:37,369 --> 01:38:39,622
I'm emotional right now,
but because I'm happy.

2102
01:38:39,705 --> 01:38:41,165
I'm happy of the way
that I played.

2103
01:38:41,248 --> 01:38:45,002
<i>I'm happy of the experiences</i>
<i>that</i> Survivor's<i> given me,</i>

2104
01:38:45,085 --> 01:38:47,004
<i>the friendships</i>
<i>they've given me.</i>

2105
01:38:47,087 --> 01:38:48,380
<i>I don't have any regrets,</i>

2106
01:38:48,464 --> 01:38:50,507
and I wouldn't have wanted it
any other way.

2107
01:38:57,931 --> 01:39:00,392
♪ ♪

2108
01:39:00,476 --> 01:39:02,186
(howls)

2109
01:39:02,269 --> 01:39:05,648
(both howl)

2110
01:39:05,731 --> 01:39:06,857
NATALIE:
You got some news for us?

2111
01:39:06,940 --> 01:39:08,525
-You got something!
We can see it!
-What's in there?

2112
01:39:08,609 --> 01:39:10,861
-Ah!
-(squeals) Yes!

2113
01:39:10,944 --> 01:39:12,029
All right, guys.
You ready for this?

2114
01:39:12,112 --> 01:39:15,074
-Yes.
-All right, here we go.

2115
01:39:15,157 --> 01:39:16,158
"Congratulations!

2116
01:39:16,241 --> 01:39:18,661
"You have made it
to the final three.

2117
01:39:18,744 --> 01:39:19,870
-(whoops)
-"Follow the trail

2118
01:39:19,953 --> 01:39:21,914
"behind your camp

2119
01:39:21,997 --> 01:39:25,876
for your well-earned
Day 39<i> Survivor</i> breakfast."

2120
01:39:25,959 --> 01:39:27,252
Yes! We made it!

2121
01:39:27,336 --> 01:39:28,504
-Food. Let's go.
-Congratulations, guys, man.

2122
01:39:28,587 --> 01:39:30,839
-Dirty Jersey!
-Congratulations.

2123
01:39:30,923 --> 01:39:32,049
-Congratulations.
-Yay.

2124
01:39:32,132 --> 01:39:33,509
<i>MICHELE:</i>
<i>My last season,</i>

2125
01:39:33,592 --> 01:39:35,052
I achieved
the ultimate accomplishment

2126
01:39:35,135 --> 01:39:36,887
by winning<i> Survivor.</i>

2127
01:39:36,970 --> 01:39:38,847
-(whoops)
-Absolutely. (whoops)
-Let's go!

2128
01:39:38,931 --> 01:39:41,934
<i>MICHELE:</i>
<i>But I got so much feedback from</i>

2129
01:39:42,017 --> 01:39:44,561
the public
and from my fellow contestants

2130
01:39:44,645 --> 01:39:46,939
that maybe I wasn't
the most deserving person.

2131
01:39:47,022 --> 01:39:49,441
<i>It took something that was</i>
<i>my biggest accomplishment</i>

2132
01:39:49,525 --> 01:39:50,192
<i>and made it into</i>
<i>one of my toughest moments</i>

2133
01:39:50,275 --> 01:39:52,236
in my life.

2134
01:39:52,319 --> 01:39:54,279
-I don't even know
where to start.
-Yay!

2135
01:39:54,363 --> 01:39:55,614
-TONY: Is that champagne?
-MICHELE: Mm-hmm.

2136
01:39:55,698 --> 01:39:58,158
<i>But, every single day out here,</i>
<i>I proved</i>

2137
01:39:58,242 --> 01:40:00,160
<i>to myself that I think I am</i>

2138
01:40:00,244 --> 01:40:02,204
<i>one of the very, very best</i>
<i>in this game.</i>

2139
01:40:02,287 --> 01:40:04,748
-Ooh! What?
-(yelps)

2140
01:40:04,832 --> 01:40:06,250
<i>MICHELE:</i>
<i>I've been on the bottom,</i>

2141
01:40:06,333 --> 01:40:08,877
constantly having
to fight my way out of it.

2142
01:40:08,961 --> 01:40:11,255
<i>And now, here I am again,</i>
<i>in the final three,</i>

2143
01:40:11,338 --> 01:40:14,883
and I feel like
this has closed a wound

2144
01:40:14,967 --> 01:40:16,927
that has been open for me
for a while.

2145
01:40:17,010 --> 01:40:19,763
<i>And I will go in tonight</i>
<i>and make sure that I do</i>

2146
01:40:19,847 --> 01:40:21,557
my darnedest to win.

2147
01:40:21,640 --> 01:40:23,934
May the best man or woman win.

2148
01:40:24,017 --> 01:40:25,436
-Congratulations, guys. Cheers.
-Cheers.

2149
01:40:25,519 --> 01:40:27,730
<i>NATALIE:</i>
<i>Even though I have</i>

2150
01:40:27,813 --> 01:40:30,107
a very nontraditional path
to the final three,

2151
01:40:30,190 --> 01:40:33,277
<i>I took the hand I was dealt</i>
<i>and said, "You know what?</i>

2152
01:40:33,360 --> 01:40:35,028
<i>"I'm gonna play the best damn</i>

2153
01:40:35,112 --> 01:40:36,947
Extinction game I can."

2154
01:40:37,030 --> 01:40:38,449
Bacon! Oh, my God.

2155
01:40:38,532 --> 01:40:40,117
Okay, so I'm gonna do
a fried egg. I can't wait.

2156
01:40:40,200 --> 01:40:42,327
<i>I knew that I had the grit,</i>

2157
01:40:42,411 --> 01:40:45,622
<i>that I had the strength</i>
<i>and the willpower</i>

2158
01:40:45,706 --> 01:40:47,124
<i>to do what it takes.</i>

2159
01:40:47,207 --> 01:40:48,792
<i>I never gave up,</i>
<i>and I was relentless</i>

2160
01:40:48,876 --> 01:40:51,128
<i>in my effort to come back</i>
<i>into the game.</i>

2161
01:40:51,211 --> 01:40:53,046
Oh, look at that.
Look at-- Oh!

2162
01:40:53,130 --> 01:40:54,506
<i>NATALIE:</i>
<i>The most important thing I have</i>

2163
01:40:54,590 --> 01:40:56,967
<i>to get across to the jury</i>
<i>is to prove to the people</i>

2164
01:40:57,050 --> 01:40:58,635
<i>that don't believe in me</i>

2165
01:40:58,719 --> 01:41:01,013
I was able to duke it out
with the best of the best

2166
01:41:01,096 --> 01:41:01,972
and I came out on top.

2167
01:41:02,055 --> 01:41:03,766
<i>So I'm going to be confident,</i>

2168
01:41:03,849 --> 01:41:05,142
<i>be proud, and prove</i>

2169
01:41:05,225 --> 01:41:08,479
that I deserve this $2 million.

2170
01:41:08,562 --> 01:41:10,355
-TONY: Are you guys excited
for tonight?
-NATALIE/MICHELE: Yeah.

2171
01:41:10,439 --> 01:41:13,150
-What a journey, huh?
-NATALIE/MICHELE: Yeah.

2172
01:41:13,233 --> 01:41:16,153
<i>TONY: This is an opportunity</i>
<i>to win a second time and prove</i>

2173
01:41:16,236 --> 01:41:19,239
that I'm one of the greatest
players to ever play this game.

2174
01:41:19,323 --> 01:41:21,366
<i>Everybody has</i>
<i>their own specialty</i>

2175
01:41:21,450 --> 01:41:23,410
<i>and what they're focused on--</i>
<i>they're good at challenges,</i>

2176
01:41:23,494 --> 01:41:24,995
they're good at the social game,

2177
01:41:25,078 --> 01:41:26,497
they're good
at the strategic game.

2178
01:41:26,580 --> 01:41:28,081
<i>But, me,</i>
<i>I do a little of everything.</i>

2179
01:41:28,165 --> 01:41:28,665
<i>And that's what it takes</i>
<i>to be a great player.</i>

2180
01:41:28,749 --> 01:41:30,375
<i>You have to be good at</i>

2181
01:41:30,459 --> 01:41:32,336
everything<i> Survivor</i> has
to throw your way.

2182
01:41:32,419 --> 01:41:34,296
Last day on Survivor Island.

2183
01:41:34,379 --> 01:41:36,298
You got to just
take it all in, right?

2184
01:41:36,381 --> 01:41:39,843
<i>These are all winners.</i>
<i>These are the best of the best.</i>

2185
01:41:39,927 --> 01:41:40,844
<i>And these jurors--</i>

2186
01:41:40,928 --> 01:41:42,179
I had a big part
of ruining their chances

2187
01:41:42,262 --> 01:41:44,348
of winning $2 million
to better their families.

2188
01:41:44,431 --> 01:41:46,308
<i>So I know the pain</i>
<i>that they're feeling.</i>

2189
01:41:46,391 --> 01:41:48,310
<i>The wounds are deep,</i>
<i>and I know they're real.</i>

2190
01:41:48,393 --> 01:41:50,395
<i>So this is gonna be</i>
<i>the hardest task of all,</i>

2191
01:41:50,479 --> 01:41:53,190
to try to convince them
that I deserve

2192
01:41:53,273 --> 01:41:55,442
<i>the title of Sole Survivor.</i>

2193
01:41:55,526 --> 01:41:58,987
<i>But I'm pretty confident</i>
<i>in how I played my game.</i>

2194
01:41:59,071 --> 01:42:00,989
So, we always had
a queen of<i> Survivor</i>

2195
01:42:01,073 --> 01:42:01,907
for many, many years,
which was Sandra.

2196
01:42:01,990 --> 01:42:05,035
<i>We never had</i>
<i>a king of</i> Survivor.

2197
01:42:05,118 --> 01:42:07,204
Now I'm hoping that I can
take it home and be the king.

2198
01:42:07,287 --> 01:42:10,207
(thunder rumbling)

2199
01:42:10,290 --> 01:42:11,291
♪ ♪

2200
01:42:37,818 --> 01:42:38,402
PROBST:
All right.

2201
01:42:38,485 --> 01:42:41,029
Natalie, Tony, Michele,

2202
01:42:41,113 --> 01:42:43,240
let's get to your final
Tribal Council.

2203
01:42:43,323 --> 01:42:47,911
It is only fitting that this war
would come to an end

2204
01:42:47,995 --> 01:42:50,080
under a torrential downpour.

2205
01:42:50,163 --> 01:42:52,124
You guys have had a lot
to deal with this year:

2206
01:42:52,207 --> 01:42:54,877
20 winners; the introduction
of a fire token,

2207
01:42:54,960 --> 01:42:56,795
which birthed
a<i> Survivor</i> economy,

2208
01:42:56,879 --> 01:43:00,048
complete with a supply
and demand of advantages;

2209
01:43:00,132 --> 01:43:03,093
and Edge of Extinction,
which is playing out tonight.

2210
01:43:03,176 --> 01:43:05,095
Natalie earned her way
back into this game.

2211
01:43:05,178 --> 01:43:07,264
Your final battle
is against each other,

2212
01:43:07,347 --> 01:43:10,267
and it is to persuade this jury

2213
01:43:10,350 --> 01:43:13,437
that you are the most deserving
of the title of Sole Survivor

2214
01:43:13,520 --> 01:43:17,441
and the record-setting
$2 million prize

2215
01:43:17,524 --> 01:43:19,151
that comes with it.

2216
01:43:19,234 --> 01:43:20,611
All right, let's get started

2217
01:43:20,694 --> 01:43:22,738
with the outwit portion
of the game.

2218
01:43:22,821 --> 01:43:23,447
This is the social part
of the game--

2219
01:43:23,530 --> 01:43:26,283
the alliances, relationships.

2220
01:43:26,366 --> 01:43:28,285
You guys have talked a lot
about previous friendships,

2221
01:43:28,368 --> 01:43:29,411
how that might have factored in,

2222
01:43:29,494 --> 01:43:31,955
morality and ethics,
if that was important to you.

2223
01:43:32,039 --> 01:43:33,457
Who wants to get us going?

2224
01:43:33,540 --> 01:43:35,083
YUL:
All right.

2225
01:43:35,167 --> 01:43:37,169
Getting a little stage fright,
Jeff, but here goes.

2226
01:43:37,252 --> 01:43:38,420
Wait a minute.

2227
01:43:38,503 --> 01:43:41,131
-(others chuckling)
-You've been on<i> Survivor</i> twice,

2228
01:43:41,214 --> 01:43:42,966
-and you have stage fright?
-I mean,

2229
01:43:43,050 --> 01:43:44,801
you know, I'm just feeling,
kind of, pressure, but...

2230
01:43:44,885 --> 01:43:46,970
-Go for it, Yul. Do it, Yul.
-All right, good.
All right, ready?

2231
01:43:47,054 --> 01:43:48,347
-PARVATI: You can do it, Yul.
-YUL: Can we go? All right.
-Yul, get us started.

2232
01:43:48,430 --> 01:43:51,600
-(Danni laughs)
-Cool. All right. Before
we jump in with questions,

2233
01:43:51,683 --> 01:43:54,311
I just really want
to offer you huge kudos

2234
01:43:54,394 --> 01:43:57,147
and congratulate you guys
for playing a-a great game

2235
01:43:57,230 --> 01:43:58,231
and getting to the end.

2236
01:43:58,315 --> 01:44:01,151
I mean, all of you took
a completely unique path,

2237
01:44:01,234 --> 01:44:02,194
encountering
different obstacles.

2238
01:44:02,277 --> 01:44:03,487
So, tonight,
what we really need is

2239
01:44:03,570 --> 01:44:06,198
for you to fill in
the missing blanks

2240
01:44:06,281 --> 01:44:09,117
so that we have a coherent
narrative of how you outwitted

2241
01:44:09,201 --> 01:44:12,162
all of us to be sitting
where you are right now.

2242
01:44:12,245 --> 01:44:16,124
And, on behalf of all of us,
I wish you the best of luck.

2243
01:44:16,208 --> 01:44:17,167
So much for stage fright.

2244
01:44:17,250 --> 01:44:17,834
-(laughter)
-Right.

2245
01:44:17,918 --> 01:44:19,962
DENISE:
Jeff, I'll start.

2246
01:44:20,045 --> 01:44:21,338
All right. Denise.

2247
01:44:21,421 --> 01:44:22,673
DENISE:
What I'm curious to know is:

2248
01:44:22,756 --> 01:44:26,218
What areas would you identify as
missteps or missed opportunities

2249
01:44:26,301 --> 01:44:27,344
related to the social aspect

2250
01:44:27,427 --> 01:44:29,721
that you need
to play in the game?

2251
01:44:29,805 --> 01:44:31,640
-Natalie.
-NATALIE: Okay.

2252
01:44:31,723 --> 01:44:34,393
I think my misstep
was definitely my day one.

2253
01:44:34,476 --> 01:44:36,478
I think I relied on my outplay

2254
01:44:36,561 --> 01:44:40,023
and my strength
for people to see me

2255
01:44:40,107 --> 01:44:40,816
as an asset to their tribe,

2256
01:44:40,899 --> 01:44:43,527
and I did not go to people
and say,

2257
01:44:43,610 --> 01:44:45,988
"Hey, like, I want
to kind of get to know you."

2258
01:44:46,071 --> 01:44:49,199
And it was a missed opportunity
on my part,

2259
01:44:49,282 --> 01:44:50,826
not reaching out more
that day one.

2260
01:44:50,909 --> 01:44:55,205
And that obviously led me
to getting voted off.

2261
01:44:55,288 --> 01:44:57,457
-How 'bout you, Michele?
-MICHELE: Well, I had
a lot of really great

2262
01:44:57,541 --> 01:44:58,500
one-on-one alliances.

2263
01:44:58,583 --> 01:45:02,170
I found the people
who kept me safe

2264
01:45:02,254 --> 01:45:04,214
and kept my name
out of the votes

2265
01:45:04,297 --> 01:45:05,549
and people
who I really relied on.

2266
01:45:05,632 --> 01:45:07,300
And that's great.

2267
01:45:07,384 --> 01:45:09,261
But if you don't have
something bigger than that,

2268
01:45:09,344 --> 01:45:09,928
you're just two people.

2269
01:45:10,012 --> 01:45:11,722
And that's why I always felt

2270
01:45:11,805 --> 01:45:13,265
like I was
kind of on the bottom,

2271
01:45:13,348 --> 01:45:15,058
because this is a numbers game
and I needed numbers.

2272
01:45:15,142 --> 01:45:18,020
Also, some of
my preexisting relationships

2273
01:45:18,103 --> 01:45:19,896
put a target on my back.

2274
01:45:19,980 --> 01:45:23,233
Yes, I had a relationship
with Wendell, but,

2275
01:45:23,316 --> 01:45:24,401
when you get on the beach, you
never know what's gonna stick

2276
01:45:24,484 --> 01:45:27,195
and what's not and how
that's actually gonna play out.

2277
01:45:27,279 --> 01:45:29,573
I don't think any of us can say

2278
01:45:29,656 --> 01:45:31,783
that this game went
as we expected.

2279
01:45:31,867 --> 01:45:34,286
-PROBST: Tony.
-TONY: Uh, y-you know what?

2280
01:45:34,369 --> 01:45:36,872
My first season, I wasn't as
open and vulnerable to people.

2281
01:45:36,955 --> 01:45:39,416
Um, soon as I hit the beach,
I was strategy and strategy.

2282
01:45:39,499 --> 01:45:40,625
But the missed opportunities
this season, I don't think

2283
01:45:40,709 --> 01:45:43,670
I had any. I think I talked
to every single one of you guys.

2284
01:45:43,754 --> 01:45:45,630
I-I was vulnerable to you guys.

2285
01:45:45,714 --> 01:45:47,924
I opened up
to every single one of youse.

2286
01:45:48,008 --> 01:45:48,967
And that's what determined

2287
01:45:49,051 --> 01:45:50,260
which way I was gonna go
into the game,

2288
01:45:50,343 --> 01:45:52,220
by knowing you guys
from the inside out.

2289
01:45:52,304 --> 01:45:53,597
NICK:
Is that okay,

2290
01:45:53,680 --> 01:45:55,974
to just do whatever
you got to do to build a bond,

2291
01:45:56,058 --> 01:45:58,226
just so that we won't
write your name down, and then,

2292
01:45:58,310 --> 01:45:59,978
no matter what you have to do
to get us out,

2293
01:46:00,062 --> 01:46:01,229
-it's worth it?
-But-but, Nick,

2294
01:46:01,313 --> 01:46:03,440
I found out
you were trying to blindside me.

2295
01:46:03,523 --> 01:46:05,442
So the bonds you and I shared
was 100% real.

2296
01:46:05,525 --> 01:46:06,943
I wanted to go
to the end with you,

2297
01:46:07,027 --> 01:46:08,445
but you didn't want
to go with me.

2298
01:46:08,528 --> 01:46:09,446
-So what about me?
-Same thing with you, Jeremy.

2299
01:46:09,529 --> 01:46:13,283
Um, I-I live a very boring
and simple life.

2300
01:46:13,366 --> 01:46:14,826
I don't, I don't travel nowhere.

2301
01:46:14,910 --> 01:46:17,120
I don't go to fine dining.

2302
01:46:17,204 --> 01:46:18,371
Sports--
I don't know nothing about.

2303
01:46:18,455 --> 01:46:21,291
But the one thing we got
close with is family bonds.

2304
01:46:21,375 --> 01:46:23,001
We had a lot of
vulnerable moments together.

2305
01:46:23,085 --> 01:46:24,252
That's all real.

2306
01:46:24,336 --> 01:46:25,754
I respect you as a man.

2307
01:46:25,837 --> 01:46:26,463
I respect you as a fireman.
I respect you as a father.

2308
01:46:26,546 --> 01:46:28,799
Can I say something?

2309
01:46:28,882 --> 01:46:29,883
I'm standing up for Jeremy

2310
01:46:29,966 --> 01:46:33,303
to say that Tony's response
to Jeremy, I think,

2311
01:46:33,386 --> 01:46:34,763
is completely false.

2312
01:46:34,846 --> 01:46:36,014
Don't say I didn't care. Don't
say about caring, all right?

2313
01:46:36,098 --> 01:46:37,474
'Cause me and him shared a lot
of intimate moments together,

2314
01:46:37,557 --> 01:46:39,476
and that was real.

2315
01:46:39,559 --> 01:46:41,144
As far as gameplay,

2316
01:46:41,228 --> 01:46:42,020
I did work with you
as far as I could.

2317
01:46:42,104 --> 01:46:43,855
But I couldn't go
any further with you

2318
01:46:43,939 --> 01:46:44,898
'cause I was scared of you.

2319
01:46:44,981 --> 01:46:47,484
I can attest for Tony's loyalty.

2320
01:46:47,567 --> 01:46:50,320
I found an idol while Tony
was sitting right next to me,

2321
01:46:50,403 --> 01:46:52,322
and he called me out on it.

2322
01:46:52,405 --> 01:46:55,367
And from that day forward,
he told me that he had my back.

2323
01:46:55,450 --> 01:46:58,328
But you're saying you're--
you could attest to his loyalty,

2324
01:46:58,411 --> 01:47:00,080
but we can't.
He voted us out.

2325
01:47:01,081 --> 01:47:03,291
ADAM:
Um, Natalie,

2326
01:47:03,375 --> 01:47:05,293
on the Edge, one job is

2327
01:47:05,377 --> 01:47:07,838
to set yourself up to be able
to get back in the game

2328
01:47:07,921 --> 01:47:10,340
and to be able to maybe have
an advantage in the game

2329
01:47:10,423 --> 01:47:12,050
if you do get back in the game.

2330
01:47:12,134 --> 01:47:14,678
There's no denying
that you absolutely crushed

2331
01:47:14,761 --> 01:47:18,181
-that part of the Edge game.
-(chuckles)

2332
01:47:18,265 --> 01:47:20,517
-NATALIE: Yeah.
-All you have to do besides that

2333
01:47:20,600 --> 01:47:21,726
is win jury votes

2334
01:47:21,810 --> 01:47:24,229
and make people
want you to win this game.

2335
01:47:24,312 --> 01:47:27,315
NATALIE:
So, when I came to Koru,

2336
01:47:27,399 --> 01:47:28,692
my first line of defense
was paint Tony

2337
01:47:28,775 --> 01:47:32,070
as the biggest threat
and make it seem like

2338
01:47:32,154 --> 01:47:33,572
I was the outcast at Extinction.

2339
01:47:33,655 --> 01:47:38,201
It was my play to paint
the picture of Extinction

2340
01:47:38,285 --> 01:47:39,870
to be whatever it was.

2341
01:47:39,953 --> 01:47:43,331
-ROB: Natalie,
if that is the case...
-Yeah.

2342
01:47:43,415 --> 01:47:45,208
...and you did go back
and say that strategically,

2343
01:47:45,292 --> 01:47:46,543
that's really smart.

2344
01:47:46,626 --> 01:47:47,878
-And I understand that.
-Yeah. Okay.

2345
01:47:47,961 --> 01:47:49,880
But for the week leading up

2346
01:47:49,963 --> 01:47:52,215
-before the battle-back...
-Yeah.

2347
01:47:52,299 --> 01:47:55,343
...why did you
completely isolate myself,

2348
01:47:55,427 --> 01:47:58,680
Amber, Ethan, Yul, Wendell?

2349
01:47:58,763 --> 01:48:02,225
All of those people
are still here on the jury.

2350
01:48:02,309 --> 01:48:04,895
There were two things
that I found before

2351
01:48:04,978 --> 01:48:08,231
I left that week-- it was
the extortion I sent to Tony

2352
01:48:08,315 --> 01:48:11,234
and the advantage
I sent to Nick.

2353
01:48:11,318 --> 01:48:13,695
Those two things
did create a rift

2354
01:48:13,778 --> 01:48:15,906
in my relationship
with everybody there because

2355
01:48:15,989 --> 01:48:19,242
it was for the first time I was
doing something super secretive,

2356
01:48:19,326 --> 01:48:21,578
and it meant
such a big deal to me

2357
01:48:21,661 --> 01:48:24,372
that I didn't know
if I wanted to tell people.

2358
01:48:24,456 --> 01:48:26,708
And, also,
when I'm focused on something

2359
01:48:26,791 --> 01:48:29,628
like the challenge,
which I was so nervous about,

2360
01:48:29,711 --> 01:48:31,630
I needed to breathe
and separate.

2361
01:48:31,713 --> 01:48:34,090
But whatever it did,
it worked for me.

2362
01:48:34,174 --> 01:48:35,550
And that's the real me.

2363
01:48:35,634 --> 01:48:37,928
Like, I know that I am
a strong personality

2364
01:48:38,011 --> 01:48:39,763
and it's not
everybody's cup of tea.

2365
01:48:39,846 --> 01:48:42,557
But I was 100% real with you
from the start,

2366
01:48:42,641 --> 01:48:44,267
and I did feel like
I got to know you.

2367
01:48:44,351 --> 01:48:47,103
And that's something
I appreciate about you, Natalie,

2368
01:48:47,187 --> 01:48:49,189
is that you don't put on an act.

2369
01:48:49,272 --> 01:48:51,900
You were always
really honest with people,

2370
01:48:51,983 --> 01:48:54,444
even if it pissed them off,
even if they didn't like it,

2371
01:48:54,527 --> 01:48:57,113
and you were out for number one
really unapologetically.

2372
01:48:57,197 --> 01:48:58,823
I want to hear from Tony.

2373
01:48:58,907 --> 01:49:00,283
We're hearing stories
from people

2374
01:49:00,367 --> 01:49:01,952
that you blindsided
and voted off,

2375
01:49:02,035 --> 01:49:04,496
and none of them
feel burned by you.

2376
01:49:04,579 --> 01:49:06,915
-ROB: You weren't even targeted.
-PARVATI: Yeah.

2377
01:49:06,998 --> 01:49:08,333
ROB:
We're fascinated.

2378
01:49:08,416 --> 01:49:10,961
-We want to know:
How did you do it?
-TONY: All right.

2379
01:49:11,044 --> 01:49:12,128
Um... (chuckles)

2380
01:49:12,212 --> 01:49:14,297
My-my first season,
I built a spy shack.

2381
01:49:14,381 --> 01:49:16,716
The second season,
I built a spy bunker.

2382
01:49:16,800 --> 01:49:17,801
(laughs): This season-- Adam,
you're gonna love this, man.

2383
01:49:17,884 --> 01:49:20,470
-Spy nest?
-TONY: Yes, man.

2384
01:49:20,553 --> 01:49:21,638
I used to climb up there

2385
01:49:21,721 --> 01:49:23,473
and listen to who wanted
to blindside me.

2386
01:49:23,556 --> 01:49:25,183
I used to have a bird's-eye view

2387
01:49:25,267 --> 01:49:27,644
-looking down
and looking at them.
-(laughter)

2388
01:49:27,727 --> 01:49:30,313
And at one point,
I was up there for, like,

2389
01:49:30,397 --> 01:49:33,566
a half hour, and I'm holding
on a twig and-and I'm shaking.

2390
01:49:33,650 --> 01:49:35,652
And I almost fell
out of the spy nest.

2391
01:49:35,735 --> 01:49:37,779
That-That's how I knew a lot
of the things that I did know,

2392
01:49:37,862 --> 01:49:40,657
which helped me, and that was
strategic part of it,

2393
01:49:40,740 --> 01:49:43,201
and the game-- let the game
evolve as it's gonna evolve.

2394
01:49:43,285 --> 01:49:45,120
WENDELL:
So, Tony, you made it to the end

2395
01:49:45,203 --> 01:49:47,455
without seeing any votes
against you. Great job.

2396
01:49:47,539 --> 01:49:50,542
Um, Natalie, you did play
a great Edge game.

2397
01:49:50,625 --> 01:49:52,002
Michele, you're
sitting here at the end.

2398
01:49:52,085 --> 01:49:53,837
You played a different game
than the two of them.

2399
01:49:53,920 --> 01:49:57,173
Can you just speak
to the outwit in your game?

2400
01:49:57,257 --> 01:49:58,842
MICHELE:
Sure, yeah. So, I got left out

2401
01:49:58,925 --> 01:50:02,512
of a lot of votes, so I kept
having to pick myself up.

2402
01:50:02,595 --> 01:50:03,847
I reintegrated.
I always put a smile on my face,

2403
01:50:03,930 --> 01:50:07,350
and it kept the target off me
a lot of the time.

2404
01:50:07,434 --> 01:50:09,644
I found cracks.
I moved within those cracks.

2405
01:50:09,728 --> 01:50:12,230
And, you know, I think I played

2406
01:50:12,314 --> 01:50:13,815
a really adaptable
and flexible game.

2407
01:50:13,898 --> 01:50:16,860
You know, Tony had these great
alliances, and they helped him.

2408
01:50:16,943 --> 01:50:20,488
I didn't really have anyone
helping me at the end.

2409
01:50:20,572 --> 01:50:23,033
It was me, alone,
when everybody was telling me

2410
01:50:23,116 --> 01:50:23,867
that I was gonna be
the next to go.

2411
01:50:23,950 --> 01:50:26,745
So, to be on the bottom
for that long,

2412
01:50:26,828 --> 01:50:30,373
it's pretty amazing
that I find myself sitting here

2413
01:50:30,457 --> 01:50:32,709
despite all my challenges.

2414
01:50:32,792 --> 01:50:34,377
BEN:
Yeah. You know,

2415
01:50:34,461 --> 01:50:35,211
as a fellow
controversial winner,

2416
01:50:35,295 --> 01:50:37,505
I realize why you won
your season.

2417
01:50:37,589 --> 01:50:39,716
And you did a heck of a job
this year,

2418
01:50:39,799 --> 01:50:41,468
and you should be very proud
of what you've done.

2419
01:50:41,551 --> 01:50:42,677
Thank you, Ben.

2420
01:50:42,761 --> 01:50:45,472
All right, you guys good to move
into the outplay portion?

2421
01:50:45,555 --> 01:50:46,556
Yeah.

2422
01:50:46,639 --> 01:50:47,682
PROBST:
Who wants to get us going?

2423
01:50:47,766 --> 01:50:49,517
You guys had a lot
to deal with this season

2424
01:50:49,601 --> 01:50:50,894
in terms of twists,

2425
01:50:50,977 --> 01:50:52,604
the fire token,
Edge of Extinction advantages

2426
01:50:52,687 --> 01:50:54,564
coming into the game.

2427
01:50:54,647 --> 01:50:57,692
Any questions in that part
of the game for these three?

2428
01:50:57,776 --> 01:50:59,027
I have a question.

2429
01:50:59,110 --> 01:51:00,653
-Natalie.
-Yeah.

2430
01:51:00,737 --> 01:51:03,073
Can you please share with us
all the things

2431
01:51:03,156 --> 01:51:05,867
that you found, won
or sent into the game?

2432
01:51:05,950 --> 01:51:09,412
Okay. So, if the social part is

2433
01:51:09,496 --> 01:51:11,581
one of my weaker parts
of the game,

2434
01:51:11,664 --> 01:51:13,416
this is definitely
one of the strengths.

2435
01:51:13,500 --> 01:51:17,796
The first one I found was
the idol that I sold to Sandra.

2436
01:51:17,879 --> 01:51:19,923
The second one was
the advantage to be able

2437
01:51:20,006 --> 01:51:22,550
to leave Tribal Council
without voting.

2438
01:51:22,634 --> 01:51:24,219
-Safety without power.
-Safety without power.

2439
01:51:24,302 --> 01:51:25,762
And I sold it to Jeremy.

2440
01:51:25,845 --> 01:51:27,931
The third one was
the one I sold to Sarah.

2441
01:51:28,014 --> 01:51:32,102
She had to sneak onto
the opposite tribe's beach

2442
01:51:32,185 --> 01:51:34,771
and steal an advantage
to have the extra vote.

2443
01:51:34,854 --> 01:51:36,564
Four was... Oh.

2444
01:51:36,648 --> 01:51:38,274
I extorted Tony
for six fire tokens.

2445
01:51:38,358 --> 01:51:41,486
The fifth one
was the Nick advantage

2446
01:51:41,569 --> 01:51:43,571
where he could disadvantage
somebody else.

2447
01:51:43,655 --> 01:51:44,697
The other two things

2448
01:51:44,781 --> 01:51:46,866
that everybody else
got an option to do was

2449
01:51:46,950 --> 01:51:49,244
the log challenge
and the coconut challenge.

2450
01:51:49,327 --> 01:51:51,079
Those two were
the hardest challenges

2451
01:51:51,162 --> 01:51:52,872
I've ever had to do.

2452
01:51:52,956 --> 01:51:56,626
Nonstop grinding
for one freaking fire token.

2453
01:51:56,709 --> 01:51:59,462
I was exhausted
and broken after both.

2454
01:51:59,546 --> 01:52:02,966
For me, it was really cool
to be sitting at Tribal Council,

2455
01:52:03,049 --> 01:52:06,970
watching the advantages
and disadvantages I sent over,

2456
01:52:07,053 --> 01:52:08,972
kind of being a part of the game

2457
01:52:09,055 --> 01:52:12,142

physically being on the island.

2458
01:52:12,225 --> 01:52:14,978
It was my way of playing
<i>Survivor</i> out on the Edge,

2459

the things that I would do

2460

BEN:
Winning an immunity challenge

2462

The challenges is how

2464

Tony, you won four challenges
this year,

2465
01:52:30,618 --> 01:52:32,662

Michele, you won two this year.

Can you guys talk about
the will and the drive

2470

my all to win that necklace.

2471

"Wow, I<i> could</i> win challenges."

2472

And that's when I went to win

2473

I shouldn't even have
let you get that, man.

2474
01:52:49,596 --> 01:52:51,556
-(Tony chuckles)
-That was mine.
I should've let you

2475
01:52:51,639 --> 01:52:53,516
-sit out of it.
-MICHELE: I-I will say, like,

2476
01:52:53,600 --> 01:52:55,018
winning those immunity
challenges at clutch times,

2477

maybe a day in this game.

2478
01:52:59,606 --> 01:53:00,690
But a day changes everything.

2479
01:53:00,773 --> 01:53:02,692
Things shift so fast that I knew

2480
01:53:02,775 --> 01:53:05,862

2481
01:53:05,945 --> 01:53:08,364

everything, and it did.

2482

Things changed majorly

2483

I have a question for Natalie.

01:53:15,622 --> 01:53:17,081
When it got down to four...

2487

2488

You want to take out Tony
because everybody

2489

01:53:27,800 --> 01:53:29,010

When I won

in that moment.

2495

But I knew, at the same time,
that sitting next to Tony was

2496

2497

But, also, part of me

2498
01:53:47,654 --> 01:53:50,240

2499
01:53:50,323 --> 01:53:52,867
Basically, I wanted to finish
them off, the whole alliance,

2500
01:53:52,951 --> 01:53:54,410

2501
01:53:54,494 --> 01:53:55,411
At the end of the day,

2502
01:53:55,495 --> 01:53:59,082

It was what I chose to do,

2504

01:54:03,044 --> 01:54:05,797
ETHAN:
Tony, Michele,
uh, like, what are

01:54:05,880 --> 01:54:07,715

How do you feel

01:54:09,467 --> 01:54:11,719

The Edge, it's awesome

01:54:13,721 --> 01:54:16,057
But the only thing

2511
01:54:16,140 --> 01:54:17,058

2512

When I first read that thing,

2513
01:54:18,810 --> 01:54:21,396
I was so excited. I was like,
"I get to extort somebody."

2514

I was so happy,
and then it says,

2516

-(laughter)
-It was, like, instant.

2517

I had two things.
I had a disadvantage,

2518
01:54:28,069 --> 01:54:29,612
and I had Natalie coming back,
saying, "Hey, guys,

2519
01:54:29,696 --> 01:54:31,281
"you got to get rid of Tony,
'cause everybody say

2520
01:54:31,364 --> 01:54:32,782
he's gonna win."
And I was like,

2521
01:54:32,865 --> 01:54:34,242
"Guys, please
don't listen to her.

2522
01:54:34,325 --> 01:54:35,618
-Please don't listen.
She's lying."
-NATALIE: Well, we had...

2523
01:54:35,702 --> 01:54:36,786
-TONY: "She's lying.
She wants to break us."
-(chuckles)

2524
01:54:36,869 --> 01:54:38,997
-NATALIE: We had the...
-So, that-that's the two things

2525
01:54:39,080 --> 01:54:40,623

2526
01:54:40,707 --> 01:54:42,292
MICHELE:
For me, I always viewed the Edge

2527
01:54:42,375 --> 01:54:43,501

2528

It either, "A," gave me

2529

2530

2531
01:54:49,716 --> 01:54:53,970

2532
01:54:54,053 --> 01:54:55,972

2533

So, everything great

2534

2535

When you guys willed me
your fire tokens and allowed me

2536
01:55:05,064 --> 01:55:07,191

strength in this game.

2537

And then Natalie coming back in

2539
01:55:11,738 --> 01:55:13,656

I-I have a chance."

2540
01:55:13,740 --> 01:55:16,284
So, for me,
that was a complete opportunity.

2541
01:55:16,367 --> 01:55:18,286
And we worked through this game,

2542
01:55:18,369 --> 01:55:20,038

2543
01:55:22,749 --> 01:55:23,833

All right.

Natalie, go first.

2550
01:55:38,598 --> 01:55:41,726

So, my journey on<i> Survivor</i> was

2551

a hand that I did not know
I was gonna be dealt.

2552

And I think on<i> Survivor,</i>

2553

to adapt and move on.

2554
01:55:49,233 --> 01:55:52,570
And when I came back in,
all I wanted to do was focus on

2555
01:55:52,654 --> 01:55:54,489

2556

2557

2558

2559

Everybody said, "It's not

2563

and you made it to the end.

2564
01:56:13,966 --> 01:56:17,053
You basically have to play
a perfect game."

2565
01:56:17,136 --> 01:56:18,221
And, so,
I'm really proud of my game.

2566
01:56:18,304 --> 01:56:20,973
I'm really excited to be here.

2567
01:56:21,057 --> 01:56:22,100
And I... I...

2568
01:56:22,183 --> 01:56:25,228
Yeah. I'm really...
I'm really excited and proud,

2569

(chuckles)

Michele.

Uh, so, my first season

I only went
to six Tribal Councils.

2575

On this season, I went
to 15 out of 19 Tribal Councils,

2576
01:56:41,869 --> 01:56:43,871

2577

2578

this season to get to the end.

2579
01:56:49,502 --> 01:56:52,797
I'm pretty proud of the way
that I played this game.

2580
01:56:52,880 --> 01:56:55,591
I think I played with integrity.

2581
01:56:55,675 --> 01:56:57,760

a-a lot of great relationships.

2582

2583

2586

it's not in my wheelhouse.

2587

2588
01:57:12,233 --> 01:57:14,610
I played that game,

2589
01:57:14,694 --> 01:57:17,280

2590
01:57:17,363 --> 01:57:19,991

2591
01:57:20,450 --> 01:57:21,909
PROBST:
Tony.

2592
01:57:21,993 --> 01:57:23,327
All right.
Me, I came into this game

01:57:23,411 --> 01:57:24,871

2596

2597

2600

2602
01:57:42,889 --> 01:57:44,307

2603

2604
01:57:46,851 --> 01:57:48,311
It took me 26 days to find one.

2605
01:57:48,394 --> 01:57:50,188
Um, the spy nest was very
helpful with my surveillance.

2606
01:57:50,271 --> 01:57:53,316
Everything I did,

2607
01:57:53,399 --> 01:57:54,317
I was leading votes

2608

2609

Natalie came in from Extinction.
She told everybody,

2610
01:57:58,738 --> 01:57:59,322

Tony's got to go.

2611
01:57:59,405 --> 01:58:01,324
He's a big threat to win."

2612
01:58:01,407 --> 01:58:02,492
Uh, she was pushing the buttons,

2613

this game.

01:58:06,412 --> 01:58:08,998
It was a tough battle

2616
01:58:09,081 --> 01:58:11,167
I know it's a big, huge,
Super Bowl season of<i> Survivor,</i>

2617

I think all three of you guys

2621
01:58:22,720 --> 01:58:23,304

2622
01:58:23,387 --> 01:58:25,264
All different games.

2623
01:58:25,348 --> 01:58:27,475
But, honestly, in my eyes,

2624
01:58:27,558 --> 01:58:28,684

2625
01:58:28,768 --> 01:58:31,687

2626
01:58:31,771 --> 01:58:34,398
-Yep. Agreed.
-She speaks for all of us.
We have huge respect

2627
01:58:34,482 --> 01:58:36,359

that got you here.

2628

ADAM:
You guys should all be
incredibly proud

2629
01:58:40,279 --> 01:58:42,198
-of yourselves
for making it there.
-Yeah.

2630
01:58:42,281 --> 01:58:43,366
Something none of us could do.

2631
01:58:43,449 --> 01:58:48,246
And tonight, each and every one
of you has fought up here,

2632
01:58:48,329 --> 01:58:50,706

all of our decisions...

2633
01:58:50,790 --> 01:58:52,083
-Awful.
-Really tough.

2634
01:58:52,166 --> 01:58:53,501
-...immensely difficult.
-Really, really hard.

2635
01:58:53,584 --> 01:58:56,212
ROB:
Because even though
some of us may have come in

2636
01:58:56,295 --> 01:58:58,756
with some ideas
of what we're gonna do,

2637
01:58:58,840 --> 01:59:01,050
tonight, you guys have
all showed why

2638
01:59:01,133 --> 01:59:04,262
each and every one of you
deserve to be up there.

2639
01:59:05,805 --> 01:59:08,349
-Yay! Good job!
-Yeah!

2640
01:59:08,432 --> 01:59:12,562
PARVATI:
So proud of you!

2641
01:59:13,980 --> 01:59:15,690
You guys deserve this.

2642
01:59:21,487 --> 01:59:24,407
PROBST:
Okay. Well, you guys have played

2643
01:59:24,490 --> 01:59:28,286

2644
01:59:28,369 --> 01:59:29,328

2645
01:59:29,412 --> 01:59:32,373

2646
01:59:32,456 --> 01:59:35,084

2647

>> Probst: ALL RIGHT, IT IS
TIME TO BRING THE 40th

2653
02:00:19,295 --> 02:00:32,016
♪
♪
♪

2659

GAME, THE FIRST TIME I WROTE IT

2660

I'M SO PROUD OF YOU.

AND WHAT YOU HAVE ACCOMPLISHED.

2663
02:01:02,546 --> 02:01:10,429
SO YOU'RE AWESOME.

02:01:15,267 --> 02:01:25,569
♪
♪
♪
♪
♪

02:01:43,295 --> 02:01:58,144
♪
♪
♪

02:01:58,227 --> 02:01:58,561
♪
♪
♪
>> Probst: I'LL GO GET THE

VOTES.

MICHELE, JURY, I WILL SEE YOU

THEY SHOULD BE A PART OF THIS.

2683
02:03:30,402 --> 02:03:30,820
BRING THEM INTO THE FRAME.

2684
02:03:30,903 --> 02:03:32,196
>> COME ON OVER HERE.

2685
02:03:32,279 --> 02:03:34,615
>> Probst: THERE'S TONY'S
FAMILY.

2686
02:03:34,698 --> 02:03:37,868
TONY, YOU'VE GOT MICHELE'S
SISTER.

2687
02:03:37,952 --> 02:03:38,410
SLIDE OVER, NATALIE.

2688
02:03:38,494 --> 02:03:41,789
A LITTLE MORE NATALIE.

2689
02:03:41,872 --> 02:03:43,666
THERE WE GO.

2690
02:03:43,749 --> 02:03:44,333
NATALIE'S BOYFRIEND.

2691
02:03:44,416 --> 02:03:45,209
LET'S PUT UP SOME MUSIC, JOE.

2692
02:03:45,292 --> 02:03:47,586
BECAUSE HERE'S THE TRUTH--
>> OH, MY GOD!

2693
02:03:47,670 --> 02:03:50,297
>> Probst: TWO OF YOU ARE
GOING TO LOSE.

2694
02:03:50,381 --> 02:03:53,676
THAT'S WHY IT'S SO VALUABLE AND
SO IMPORTANT WHEN YOU WIN.

2695
02:03:53,759 --> 02:03:54,844
IT MEANS SO MUCH.

2696
02:03:54,927 --> 02:03:58,681
ONE OF YOU IS GOING TO EARN $2
MILLION AND BECOME ONLY THE

2697
02:03:58,764 --> 02:04:03,686
SECOND TWO-TIME WINNER IN THE
HISTORY OF "SURVIVOR."

2698
02:04:03,769 --> 02:04:09,108
FOR THE FIRST TIME EVER, I'LL
READ THE VOTES FROM MY GARAGE.

2699
02:04:09,191 --> 02:04:11,193
>> OH, MY GOD!

2700
02:04:11,277 --> 02:04:13,696
>> Probst: HERE WE GO.

2701
02:04:13,779 --> 02:04:21,996
FIRST VOTE, TONY.

2702
02:04:22,079 --> 02:04:22,705
NATALIE.

2703
02:04:22,788 --> 02:04:27,668
ONE VOTE TONY, ONE VOTE NATALIE.

2704
02:04:27,751 --> 02:04:28,419
NATALIE.

2705
02:04:28,502 --> 02:04:35,718
TWO VOTES NATALIE, ONE VOTE
TONY.

2706
02:04:35,801 --> 02:04:36,510
TIED AGAIN.

2707
02:04:36,594 --> 02:04:43,726
TWO VOTES TONY, TWO VOTES
NATALIE.

2708
02:04:43,809 --> 02:04:44,560
NATALIE.

2709
02:04:44,643 --> 02:04:50,900
THREE VOTES NATALIE, TWO VOTES
TONY.

2710
02:04:50,983 --> 02:04:51,734
TIED AGAIN.

2711
02:04:51,817 --> 02:04:58,949
THREE VOTES TONY, THREE VOTES
NATALIE.

2712
02:04:59,033 --> 02:04:59,783
NATALIE.

2713
02:04:59,867 --> 02:05:05,206
FOUR VOTES NATALIE, THREE VOTES
TONY.

2714
02:05:05,289 --> 02:05:08,500
WE'RE TIED AGAIN.

2715
02:05:08,584 --> 02:05:14,590
FOUR VOTES TONY, FOUR VOTES
NATALIE.

2716
02:05:14,673 --> 02:05:15,507
TONY.

2717
02:05:15,591 --> 02:05:21,931
THAT'S FIVE VOTES TONY, FOUR
VOTES NATALIE.

2718
02:05:22,014 --> 02:05:22,848
TONY.

2719
02:05:22,932 --> 02:05:29,438
THAT'S SIX VOTES TONY, FOUR
VOTES NATALIE.

2720
02:05:29,521 --> 02:05:36,070
SEVEN VOTES TONY, FOUR VOTES
NATALIE.

2721
02:05:36,153 --> 02:05:42,284
EIGHT VOTES TONY, FOUR VOTES
NATALIE.

2722
02:05:42,368 --> 02:05:47,748
THE WINNER OF "SURVIVOR: WINNERS
AT WAR", TONY!

2723
02:05:47,831 --> 02:05:50,793
CONGRATULATIONS, TONY!

2724
02:05:50,876 --> 02:05:53,754
THERE'S OUR WINNER, AND THAT IS
THE TRUTH OF "SURVIVOR."

2725
02:05:53,837 --> 02:05:57,299
YOU HAVE THE AGONY OF DEFEAT,
AND YOU HAVE THE BEAUTIFUL WIN.

2726
02:05:57,383 --> 02:06:00,803
LET'S SEE THAT FAMILY BIG UP
THERE ON THE SCREEN.

2727
02:06:00,886 --> 02:06:06,141
TEAM TONY WITH HIS WIFE, TWO
KIDS.

2728
02:06:06,225 --> 02:06:10,813
IT'S SO HARD TO SAY GOODBYE TO
MICHELE AND NATALIE.

2729
02:06:10,896 --> 02:06:12,147
LET'S SEE HOW EVERYBODY VOTED.

2730
02:06:12,231 --> 02:06:14,191
YOU CAN SEE THERE WERE TWO
CAMPS.

2731
02:06:14,275 --> 02:06:18,654
NATALIE HAD FOUR PEOPLE WITH
HER, INCLUDING JEREMY, WHO WAS

2732
02:06:18,737 --> 02:06:19,363
LATE TO "THE EDGE."

2733
02:06:19,446 --> 02:06:20,823
AND EVERYBODY ELSE WAS FOR TONY.

2734
02:06:20,906 --> 02:06:22,825
AND DESPITE PLAYING THEIR HEARTS
OUT, THIS WAS A DOMINANT WIN,

2735
02:06:22,908 --> 02:06:23,826
TONY.

2736
02:06:23,909 --> 02:06:28,831
KIDS, IF I COULD JUST TALK TO
YOUR DAD A MINUTE.

2737
02:06:28,914 --> 02:06:31,834
REQUEST THE LITTLE BIT OF TIME
WE HAVE, TONY, HOW MUCH DOES THE

2738
02:06:31,917 --> 02:06:34,336
$2 MILLION CHANGE YOUR LIFE?

2739
02:06:34,420 --> 02:06:35,879
WE JUST HAVE A FEW SECONDS.

2740
02:06:35,963 --> 02:06:41,844
>> JEFF, IT'S LIFE CHANGINGSING,
ON IN THE WORLD, YOU SEE HOW

2741
02:06:41,927 --> 02:06:47,850
FINANCIAL SECURITY IS SO
IMPORTANT.

2742
02:06:47,933 --> 02:06:50,853
WITH THIS MONEY I'M GOING TO
MAKE SURE I SECURE MY FAMILY AND

2743
02:06:50,936 --> 02:06:52,855
BE FINANCIALLY SECURE FOR THE
REST OF MY LIFE.

2744
02:06:52,938 --> 02:06:56,358
>> Probst: TONY, I'M SORRY IT
WAS SO SHORT.

2745
02:06:56,442 --> 02:06:57,693
IT WAS AN EPIC FINALE.

2746
02:06:57,776 --> 02:07:01,488
YOU WERE A GREAT WINNER, A GREAT
REPRESENTATIVE OF OUR SHOW.

2747
02:07:01,572 --> 02:07:02,656
>> THANK YOU,.

2748
02:07:02,740 --> 02:07:06,285
>> Probst: I FEEL LIKE SUCH A
RUDE HOST.

2749
02:07:06,368 --> 02:07:08,037
HERE'S THE $2 MILLION CHECK.

2750
02:07:08,120 --> 02:07:11,040
LET'S TALK ABOUT OUR 41st
SEASON, BECAUSE NORMALLY WE SHOW

2751
02:07:11,123 --> 02:07:12,249
YOU A COOL PROMO.

2752
02:07:12,333 --> 02:07:15,878
FOR OBVIOUS REASONS WE HAVEN'T
BEEN ABLE TO SHOOT, BUT, MAN, WE

2753
02:07:15,961 --> 02:07:17,046
HAVE FUN IDEAS.

2754
02:07:17,129 --> 02:07:19,757
WE'RE ALWAYS TRYING TO EXPLORE
AND EVOLVE THE SHOW AND TAKE

2755
02:07:19,840 --> 02:07:23,177
CHANCES AND WE'RE GOING TO DO
THAT AND WE'RE COMMITTED TO

2756
02:07:23,260 --> 02:07:25,888
BEING ON THE FALL FOR OUR 41st
SEASON, WHICH MEANS YOU SHOULD

2757
02:07:25,971 --> 02:07:31,602
APPLY, FEPS YOU'RE YOUNG-- I'M
TALKING TEENAGERS, 6, 17, 18,

2758
02:07:31,685 --> 02:07:31,894
19.

2759
02:07:31,977 --> 02:07:32,936
DO IT.

2760
02:07:33,020 --> 02:07:35,230
COOL PARENTS AND A COOL SCHOOL,
WHO KNOWS IT COULD.

2761
02:07:35,314 --> 02:07:40,903
YOU CAN BID ON PROPS FOR THIS
SEASON, PROCEEDS GO TO STAND UP

2762
02:07:40,986 --> 02:07:43,906
TO CANCER, AND FEED AMERICA.

2763
02:07:43,989 --> 02:07:47,910
ON BEHALF OF OUR ENTIRE CREW,
400 PEOPLE, 25 COUNTRIES, WE

2764
02:07:47,993 --> 02:07:48,911
LOVE OUR JOBS.

2765
02:07:48,994 --> 02:07:49,912
WE'RE GOING TO COME TO YOU WITH
MORE "SURVIVOR."

2766
02:07:49,995 --> 02:07:53,791
THANK YOU, GOOD NIGHT, STAY
SAFE.

2767
02:08:07,721 --> 02:08:09,098

2768

## S41E13

1
00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:04,162
WWW.MY-SUBS.CO

1
00:00:02,061 --> 00:00:05,073
Dès le premier jour,
le rythme a été implacable.

2
00:00:05,198 --> 00:00:07,012
Ils ont survécu
avec peu de nourriture,

3
00:00:07,137 --> 00:00:09,508
ont dû faire face
aux plus dangereux rebondissements

4
00:00:09,633 --> 00:00:11,082
jamais mis dans le jeu.

5
00:00:11,207 --> 00:00:12,644
Ils roulent sur la réserve.

6
00:00:12,769 --> 00:00:15,648
Mais c'est "Survivor".
Et toute bataille épique

7
00:00:15,773 --> 00:00:18,006
a besoin de cette poussée finale.

8
00:00:18,131 --> 00:00:21,068
C'est le début de la leur.
Encore une fois, ils redémarrent.

9
00:00:21,193 --> 00:00:23,892
Nouvelle île, pas de nourriture,
pas d'abri.

10
00:00:24,017 --> 00:00:26,056
Il y aura deux épreuves d'immunité,

11
00:00:26,181 --> 00:00:27,517
deux conseils,

12
00:00:27,642 --> 00:00:29,446
une épreuve de feu.

13
00:00:29,571 --> 00:00:32,678
Et nous avons
un dernier rebondissement

14
00:00:32,803 --> 00:00:35,033
qu'ils ne verront jamais venir.

15
00:00:35,158 --> 00:00:38,427
Pour la première fois
depuis l'été 2000,

16
00:00:38,552 --> 00:00:39,942
il y a 21 ans,

17
00:00:40,349 --> 00:00:43,490
nous lirons les votes
et annoncerons le gagnant de Survivor

18
00:00:43,615 --> 00:00:44,793
ici, sur place.

19
00:00:44,918 --> 00:00:46,810
Puis nous ferons
la réunion de Survivor,

20
00:00:46,935 --> 00:00:49,373
gardant tout le monde
pour parler de la saison

21
00:00:49,498 --> 00:00:52,043
alors, qu'ils sont encore
en plein dedans.

22
00:00:52,168 --> 00:00:54,261
Les voilà, les cinq derniers.

23
00:00:54,386 --> 00:00:58,455
Deshawn, Xander, Erika,
Ricard et Heather.

24
00:00:58,580 --> 00:01:01,105
Trois iront au bout
et pourront plaider leur cause,

25
00:01:01,230 --> 00:01:04,354
expliquer pourquoi ils méritent
le titre d'Ultime Survivant

26
00:01:04,479 --> 00:01:06,604
et le million de dollars qui va avec.

27
00:01:06,729 --> 00:01:10,377
C'est la finale de Survivor 41.

28
00:01:13,269 --> 00:01:16,830
<font color="#fab419">Survivor
saison 41 épisode 13
Plus qu'une chose à faire : gagner</font>

29
00:01:25,523 --> 00:01:27,097
<i>C'est mon rêve le plus fou,</i>

30
00:01:27,222 --> 00:01:30,266
<i>je peux me voir gagner
si je conquière cette dernière étape.</i>

31
00:01:30,604 --> 00:01:32,617
<i>C'est ici et maintenant.</i>

32
00:01:32,742 --> 00:01:34,773
<i>Je dois me battre
jusqu'à la toute fin.</i>

33
00:01:35,014 --> 00:01:38,185
<i>Je me suis toujours levée et relevée,</i>

34
00:01:38,646 --> 00:01:41,300
<i>et je veux être la gagnante
la plus âgée de Survivor.</i>

35
00:01:42,387 --> 00:01:44,691
<i>Je crois à 100 % que je peux gagner.</i>

36
00:01:45,668 --> 00:01:47,566
<i>Le jeu va devenir intense.</i>

37
00:01:48,041 --> 00:01:49,985
<i>Il y aura beaucoup d'embrouilles.</i>

38
00:01:50,516 --> 00:01:52,806
<i>Il y aura beaucoup
de promesses non tenues.</i>

39
00:01:53,452 --> 00:01:55,256
<i>Ça va être une fin sauvage.</i>

40
00:02:16,353 --> 00:02:17,617
Les cinq derniers !

41
00:02:17,742 --> 00:02:18,804
C'est parti.

42
00:02:18,929 --> 00:02:20,835
Félicitations, les amis.

43
00:02:20,960 --> 00:02:22,930
<i>Jeff nous fait encore un coup tordu.</i>

44
00:02:23,055 --> 00:02:25,126
<i>On commence sur une nouvelle plage</i>

45
00:02:25,251 --> 00:02:27,623
<i>avec le strict minimum de matériel.</i>

46
00:02:27,748 --> 00:02:29,126
<i><font color="#fab419">C'est tout ce qu'on a.</font></i>

47
00:02:29,251 --> 00:02:31,023
Où est mon pantalon ?

48
00:02:31,148 --> 00:02:32,845
On doit recommencer, et...

49
00:02:34,195 --> 00:02:36,339
C'est parfait pour moi,

50
00:02:36,464 --> 00:02:39,287
car j'ai pas besoin
de manger ou dormir.

51
00:02:39,412 --> 00:02:41,426
<i>Oui, je vais manger mon adrénaline.</i>

52
00:02:41,551 --> 00:02:42,965
<i>Les autres ici,</i>

53
00:02:43,090 --> 00:02:45,457
<i>je les veux faibles,
je les veux affamés.</i>

54
00:02:45,582 --> 00:02:48,680
Ils s'effondreront
et j'irai au sommet.

55
00:02:48,805 --> 00:02:51,765
C'est pas les mêmes insectes
sur cette île et l'ancienne.

56
00:02:51,890 --> 00:02:52,859
Absolument.

57
00:02:53,276 --> 00:02:55,604
- Écoute Erika, on doit parler.
- Je...

58
00:02:55,729 --> 00:02:58,420
- Je suis désolé.
- Je suis pas prête à te parler.

59
00:02:58,545 --> 00:03:01,147
Mais n'hésite pas à dire merci
d'être encore là.

60
00:03:02,464 --> 00:03:04,635
Déclaration audacieuse.
Je t'aime, ma fille.

61
00:03:04,760 --> 00:03:07,921
J'ai juste... joué mon va-tout.
J'ai fait ce qu'il fallait.

62
00:03:08,046 --> 00:03:10,770
Je suis surprise d'avoir été
la cible de ton va-tout.

63
00:03:10,895 --> 00:03:14,005
<i>Le conseil a encore été un beau
foutoir, grâce à votre serviteur.</i>

64
00:03:14,130 --> 00:03:15,865
<i>Je devais provoquer du chaos.</i>

65
00:03:15,990 --> 00:03:19,047
Donc j'ai décidé de faire exploser
la place d'Erika, c'est tout.

66
00:03:19,172 --> 00:03:21,421
Je le dis devant tous,
que tu saches que c'est vrai.

67
00:03:21,546 --> 00:03:23,608
Erika ne t'emmènera pas
au bout, Heather.

68
00:03:23,733 --> 00:03:25,316
Elle m'a dit au puits :

69
00:03:25,441 --> 00:03:27,318
"Je ne peux pas amener
Heather à la fin."

70
00:03:27,443 --> 00:03:29,840
"Elle pourrait voler
certains de mes votes."

71
00:03:29,965 --> 00:03:32,154
Je ne comprenais jamais pourquoi

72
00:03:32,279 --> 00:03:35,418
je pouvais pas te faire confiance
à 100 %. Et maintenant, je sais.

73
00:03:35,543 --> 00:03:37,895
<i>Heather a été un peu
déconcertée par ça.</i>

74
00:03:38,020 --> 00:03:40,449
<i>Erika était énervée, à juste titre.</i>

75
00:03:40,574 --> 00:03:42,884
Que puis-je faire ?
Vous êtes au sommet, moi en bas.

76
00:03:43,009 --> 00:03:44,776
J'essaie de vous amener à mon niveau.

77
00:03:44,901 --> 00:03:46,622
C'est dur d'être en bas.

78
00:03:47,338 --> 00:03:48,805
C'est une route difficile.

79
00:03:48,930 --> 00:03:50,984
<i>Pousser les gens, c'était le but,</i>

80
00:03:51,109 --> 00:03:52,804
<i>secouer un peu la table.</i>

81
00:03:52,929 --> 00:03:55,856
Ça pourrait peut-être causer
une faille dans leur quatuor.

82
00:03:55,981 --> 00:03:57,353
Et ça l'a peut-être fait.

83
00:03:57,478 --> 00:03:59,946
- Je ne m'attendais pas à ça.
- Ouais, du tout.

84
00:04:00,071 --> 00:04:01,875
C'est pourquoi
je veux pas lui parler.

85
00:04:02,000 --> 00:04:04,357
Il dit que c'était pas personnel,
mais ça l'était.

86
00:04:04,482 --> 00:04:06,246
- Clair.
- C'était personnel.

87
00:04:06,371 --> 00:04:07,616
C'était si stupide.

88
00:04:07,741 --> 00:04:10,141
<i>Danny a été éliminé,
c'était ma décision,</i>

89
00:04:10,266 --> 00:04:12,803
<i>mais je ne ferai
plus confiance à Deshawn.</i>

90
00:04:12,928 --> 00:04:15,519
<i>Ça me rend folle,
j'ai tellement bossé</i>

91
00:04:15,644 --> 00:04:17,229
pour le protéger aujourd'hui,

92
00:04:17,354 --> 00:04:18,701
et il a juste...

93
00:04:19,279 --> 00:04:20,597
Fait caca dessus.

94
00:04:20,722 --> 00:04:23,171
Tu seras dans les quatre derniers,
et pas lui,

95
00:04:23,296 --> 00:04:24,978
car tu as fait un bon coup.

96
00:04:25,103 --> 00:04:26,579
Mais il veut t'embarrasser.

97
00:04:26,704 --> 00:04:29,844
<i>Tant que je suis dedans,
j'ai encore une chance.</i>

98
00:04:29,969 --> 00:04:32,117
L'important,
c'est comment tu rebondis.

99
00:04:32,242 --> 00:04:33,812
Donc, il doit partir.

100
00:04:33,937 --> 00:04:35,679
- Il...
- Il peut pas rester.

101
00:04:35,804 --> 00:04:37,647
Ça n'a aucun sens pour moi

102
00:04:37,772 --> 00:04:39,694
alors que j'ai essayé de...

103
00:04:40,624 --> 00:04:42,265
Le protéger tant de fois.

104
00:04:42,390 --> 00:04:44,959
<i>Deshawn pense avoir fait
quelques gros coups,</i>

105
00:04:45,084 --> 00:04:47,474
mais tout ce qu'il a fait,
c'est rendre impossible

106
00:04:47,599 --> 00:04:50,255
pour quiconque
de travailler avec lui s'il restait.

107
00:04:50,380 --> 00:04:51,825
<i>C'était parfait !</i>

108
00:04:52,349 --> 00:04:53,769
- Quoi ?
- Je sais.

109
00:04:53,894 --> 00:04:56,202
- Et regarde qui est en bas. Lui.
- Je sais.

110
00:04:56,327 --> 00:04:58,813
Je veux que Deshawn
reste le centre d'intérêt.

111
00:04:58,938 --> 00:05:00,539
D'abord pour ne pas l'être,

112
00:05:00,664 --> 00:05:03,420
<i>et pour qu'il ne soit pas
dans le carré final.</i>

113
00:05:18,220 --> 00:05:19,274
Très bien !

114
00:05:19,626 --> 00:05:20,735
Bienvenue sur

115
00:05:21,117 --> 00:05:22,960
l'émission des cinq derniers,

116
00:05:23,085 --> 00:05:25,398
présenté par Deshawn Radden.

117
00:05:25,850 --> 00:05:29,037
Ricard, qu'est-ce que ça fait
d'être le dernier membre d'Ua ?

118
00:05:29,162 --> 00:05:31,997
Pas très impressionné,
j'ai toujours su que je le serais.

119
00:05:33,137 --> 00:05:36,075
OK, ce gars est une bête,
il le savait depuis le début.

120
00:05:36,200 --> 00:05:38,572
Bien, Ricard.
Écoutez, on a regardé la saison.

121
00:05:38,697 --> 00:05:40,119
Vous êtes un grand joueur.

122
00:05:40,244 --> 00:05:42,343
<i>J'ai mis une grosse cible sur Ricard</i>

123
00:05:42,468 --> 00:05:44,871
toute la saison pour une raison
précise, pour ce moment.

124
00:05:44,996 --> 00:05:46,253
<i>Il a très bien joué.</i>

125
00:05:46,378 --> 00:05:49,455
<i>Et peut-être sont-ils assez malins
pour voir qu'il est une menace,</i>

126
00:05:49,580 --> 00:05:50,776
<i>et c'était inutile.</i>

127
00:05:50,901 --> 00:05:53,007
On veut vous voir gagner.
On est pour vous.

128
00:05:53,132 --> 00:05:55,364
Évidemment, il y a d'autres joueurs

129
00:05:55,489 --> 00:05:57,074
qui ne sont pas pour vous.

130
00:05:57,199 --> 00:05:59,644
Le type est bon dans les épreuves.

131
00:05:59,769 --> 00:06:03,719
<i>Donc, s'il ne gagne pas
la prochaine immunité, il partira.</i>

132
00:06:03,844 --> 00:06:07,042
On est excités de voir
comment ça finira. Un dernier mot ?

133
00:06:07,167 --> 00:06:07,995
<i><font color="#fab419">Non.</font></i>

134
00:06:08,120 --> 00:06:09,919
OK. On vous aime. Bonne chance.

135
00:06:11,271 --> 00:06:12,268
C'était génial.

136
00:06:13,294 --> 00:06:15,456
- Comment ça va aujourd'hui ?
- Bien.

137
00:06:17,492 --> 00:06:20,839
Sur une échelle de un à dix,
à combien es-tu énervée contre moi ?

138
00:06:22,349 --> 00:06:23,663
<font color="#fab419">Pas de commentaire.</font>

139
00:06:25,251 --> 00:06:26,494
<i>Grâce à Deshawn,</i>

140
00:06:26,619 --> 00:06:30,033
Heather est si énervée contre moi
qu'elle ne veut pas me parler.

141
00:06:30,158 --> 00:06:33,159
<i>Mais pour moi, c'est raisonnable
que chacun réfléchisse</i>

142
00:06:33,284 --> 00:06:35,862
<i>à avec qui il veut être à la fin.</i>

143
00:06:35,987 --> 00:06:39,431
<i>Je suis surprise qu'elle soit
personnellement blessée par ça.</i>

144
00:06:39,556 --> 00:06:42,568
Ça craint qu'elle ne veuille
même pas en parler.

145
00:06:42,693 --> 00:06:44,279
Utiliser un tel forum

146
00:06:44,404 --> 00:06:47,316
pour tenter
de me ridiculiser ainsi...

147
00:06:47,931 --> 00:06:50,860
Ça fait mal. Pour moi,
ça a changé notre relation.

148
00:06:50,985 --> 00:06:53,483
C'était pas mon intention.
Je voulais pas te faire mal.

149
00:06:53,608 --> 00:06:55,287
Mon raisonnement : je suis au fond.

150
00:06:55,412 --> 00:06:57,756
Oui. Et je voulais vraiment
te garder,

151
00:06:57,881 --> 00:07:00,016
je pensais qu'on avait du potentiel.

152
00:07:00,141 --> 00:07:02,633
Si tu décides de m'éliminer,
ce serait compréhensible.

153
00:07:02,758 --> 00:07:06,120
Si tu décides que je peux servir,
quoi que tu veuilles, je suis là.

154
00:07:06,245 --> 00:07:08,884
Et si tu veux rien du tout,
je comprends aussi.

155
00:07:09,009 --> 00:07:10,494
C'est comme ça. Je comprends.

156
00:07:10,619 --> 00:07:13,118
<i>Deshawn a coulé son jeu.
Il est en bas de l'échelle.</i>

157
00:07:13,243 --> 00:07:16,302
Il se raccroche à n'importe quoi,
il ne fait que lancer des grenades

158
00:07:16,427 --> 00:07:19,365
pour voir ce qu'il peut casser,
et faire sauter mon jeu.

159
00:07:19,490 --> 00:07:22,552
<i>Le truc fou,
c'est que j'espérais le garder.</i>

160
00:07:22,677 --> 00:07:24,819
Maintenant, je ne vois pas

161
00:07:24,944 --> 00:07:27,317
comment on peut aller de l'avant.

162
00:07:28,013 --> 00:07:29,746
Ça a l'air intéressant !

163
00:07:30,383 --> 00:07:32,668
<i><font color="#fab419">"Le dernier indice d'avantage."</font></i>

164
00:07:32,793 --> 00:07:33,898
Je prends.

165
00:07:34,459 --> 00:07:37,437
Les amis ! On a du courrier.

166
00:07:37,562 --> 00:07:39,442
C'est... fou.

167
00:07:39,567 --> 00:07:41,576
Il en y a un pour chacun.

168
00:07:41,701 --> 00:07:42,534
Xander.

169
00:07:42,659 --> 00:07:44,933
- Le chaos dans une enveloppe.
- Heather.

170
00:07:45,823 --> 00:07:46,912
- OK.
- Oh !

171
00:07:47,037 --> 00:07:48,343
Allons-y.

172
00:07:49,009 --> 00:07:49,825
OK !

173
00:07:50,595 --> 00:07:53,203
<i>L'indice dit : "Résolvez la phrase"</i>

174
00:07:53,328 --> 00:07:55,155
<i>"pour trouver l'avantage."</i>

175
00:07:55,280 --> 00:07:58,764
<i>"D'abord, vous devez déchiffrer
les mots, puis la phrase."</i>

176
00:07:59,205 --> 00:08:01,306
<i>"Vous ne pouvez pas
chercher l'avantage"</i>

177
00:08:01,431 --> 00:08:04,710
<i>"sans avoir correctement
résolu l'ensemble de la phrase."</i>

178
00:08:04,835 --> 00:08:06,246
<i>Ça va être difficile.</i>

179
00:08:06,371 --> 00:08:07,788
On ne connait pas l'endroit.

180
00:08:07,913 --> 00:08:10,583
Je ne sais même pas
où je suis censé faire pipi ici.

181
00:08:11,258 --> 00:08:12,834
<i>Tout le monde travaille,</i>

182
00:08:12,959 --> 00:08:15,751
<i>pour trouver comment
démêler ces mots,</i>

183
00:08:15,876 --> 00:08:17,951
<i>car quiconque aura cet avantage</i>

184
00:08:18,076 --> 00:08:21,217
aura probablement une chance
de gagner un million.

185
00:08:21,342 --> 00:08:22,841
<i>Dans ma tête, j'avais commencé</i>

186
00:08:22,966 --> 00:08:25,118
<i>à déchiffrer les mots
tout en les lisant.</i>

187
00:08:25,243 --> 00:08:26,608
<i>J'adore les puzzles !</i>

188
00:08:26,733 --> 00:08:29,124
Regardez, j'ai gagné
quatre épreuves individuelles.

189
00:08:29,249 --> 00:08:31,709
J'adore ce genre de choses,
je suis doué pour ça.

190
00:08:32,725 --> 00:08:33,629
Je l'ai.

191
00:08:35,624 --> 00:08:37,021
<i>La phrase finale est :</i>

192
00:08:37,146 --> 00:08:39,521
<i>"Votre trésor est accroché
où les arbres aiment danser."</i>

193
00:08:39,646 --> 00:08:42,966
<i>Je me dis : ils dansent près
de l'océan, ils dansent dans le vent.</i>

194
00:08:43,091 --> 00:08:45,288
<i>C'est une chasse à l'uf
à un million, là.</i>

195
00:08:45,413 --> 00:08:48,742
<i>Tout d'un coup, Xander l'a,
Ricard l'a, Deshawn l'a.</i>

196
00:08:48,867 --> 00:08:51,390
<i>En un instant, j'étais la dernière.</i>

197
00:08:51,515 --> 00:08:53,042
<font color="#fab419">Je fais le tour de ces arbres.</font>

198
00:08:53,167 --> 00:08:54,703
<font color="#fab419">- Tu regardes ceux-là ?
- Oui.</font>

199
00:08:54,828 --> 00:08:57,623
<i>Dans ma tête c'est :
"Ne laisse pas Deshawn l'avoir."</i>

200
00:08:57,748 --> 00:09:00,248
<i>C'est tout ce qui m'inquiète,
car on connait pas l'avantage.</i>

201
00:09:00,373 --> 00:09:02,963
<i>Ça pourrait être une idole,
un rebondissement au conseil.</i>

202
00:09:03,088 --> 00:09:05,977
Je crois qu'on savait tous
qu'il fallait battre Deshawn.

203
00:09:06,603 --> 00:09:09,353
Le but est que Ricard
ne trouve pas l'avantage.

204
00:09:09,478 --> 00:09:11,463
Arbres dansants, arbres dansants.

205
00:09:12,572 --> 00:09:13,928
<font color="#fab419">Trop gonflant, berk !</font>

206
00:09:14,053 --> 00:09:16,655
<i>Bien sûr, je suis la dernière
à avoir la phrase.</i>

207
00:09:16,780 --> 00:09:19,513
<i>"Votre trésor est accroché
où les arbres aiment danser."</i>

208
00:09:20,099 --> 00:09:21,731
Où dansent-ils ?

209
00:09:21,856 --> 00:09:24,770
Oh, mon Dieu !
Je déteste les chasses au trésor !

210
00:09:25,545 --> 00:09:26,488
<i>J'adore ça.</i>

211
00:09:26,613 --> 00:09:28,987
<i>C'est comme un cross,
une course sur piste.</i>

212
00:09:29,112 --> 00:09:31,041
<i>Tout le monde souffre ici,</i>

213
00:09:31,166 --> 00:09:34,558
<i>mais quand tu regardes
et vois tes adversaires grimacer,</i>

214
00:09:34,683 --> 00:09:35,837
<i>ça te booste.</i>

215
00:09:35,962 --> 00:09:39,215
<i>Tout ce que t'as à faire,
c'est de te donner encore plus.</i>

216
00:09:52,091 --> 00:09:54,159
<font color="#fab419">Mon Dieu ! Je ne pensais pas trouver.</font>

217
00:09:54,594 --> 00:09:55,706
<i>"Félicitations !"</i>

218
00:09:55,831 --> 00:09:58,380
<i>"Dans une saison où vous avez dû
tout mériter,"</i>

219
00:09:58,505 --> 00:10:01,276
<i>"vous aurez un léger avantage
dans l'épreuve d'immunité du jour."</i>

220
00:10:01,401 --> 00:10:04,315
<i>"C'est peu, mais ça pourrait
suffire. Bonne chance."</i>

221
00:10:04,440 --> 00:10:07,318
<i>Je peux pas croire
que j'ai trouvé le dernier avantage</i>

222
00:10:07,443 --> 00:10:09,825
de ce jeu complètement dingue.

223
00:10:09,950 --> 00:10:11,417
Mon Dieu, c'est peut-être

224
00:10:11,542 --> 00:10:13,232
le coup de bol que je cherchais.

225
00:10:13,357 --> 00:10:14,158
Mon Dieu.

226
00:10:14,283 --> 00:10:17,002
<i>Toutes les épreuves
ont été très serrées,</i>

227
00:10:17,127 --> 00:10:18,909
<i>donc chaque seconde compte.</i>

228
00:10:19,034 --> 00:10:22,662
Même si je n'ai qu'un
micro avantage, je le prends.

229
00:10:22,787 --> 00:10:24,866
<font color="#fab419">C'est un avantage pour l'épreuve.</font>

230
00:10:24,991 --> 00:10:26,158
<i><font color="#fab419">Tu l'as trouvé où ?</font></i>

231
00:10:26,283 --> 00:10:28,503
Dans cet arbre aux branches bizarres.

232
00:10:28,628 --> 00:10:29,593
<font color="#fab419">Cache-le !</font>

233
00:10:29,718 --> 00:10:33,272
