00:58:51,000 --> 00:58:52,275
definitely, to beat me,

1236
00:58:52,310 --> 00:58:54,482
but don't risk your spot
for that, man.

1237
00:58:54,517 --> 00:58:55,862
- I'm telling you right now.
- Yeah.

1238
00:58:55,896 --> 00:58:57,172
<i>I know Mike's plan,</i>

1239
00:58:57,206 --> 00:58:58,517
and I know what he's doing.

1240
00:58:58,551 --> 00:58:59,655
He's trying to get in my head.

1241
00:58:59,689 --> 00:59:01,551
I'm being serious.

1242
00:59:01,586 --> 00:59:03,758
If he gives you the out,
take it.

1243
00:59:03,793 --> 00:59:06,896
Mike, that's not going to work
for me, buddy.</i>

1244
00:59:06,931 --> 00:59:09,137
I love you,
but you can't get in my head.

1245
00:59:09,172 --> 00:59:11,379
You're just going
to get me hyped to beat you.

1246
00:59:19,000 --> 00:59:21,724
This is exactly what I wanted.

1247
00:59:21,758 --> 00:59:23,793
We need him, like, spooked.

1248
00:59:23,827 --> 00:59:25,448
He's practicing right now.

1249
00:59:25,482 --> 00:59:28,034
He doesn't know if he's going
against his buddy or you,

1250
00:59:28,068 --> 00:59:29,827
and I want to keep it that way. Okay.

1251
00:59:45,103 --> 00:59:47,758
<i>
I can't sit down and relax</i> <i>
and be comfortable.</i>

1252
00:59:47,793 --> 00:59:49,896
I have to be prepared to make
fire, because, in the end,

1253
00:59:49,931 --> 00:59:52,172
<i>Romeo has all the power.</i>

1254
00:59:52,206 --> 00:59:53,586
<i>He might blindside me,</i>

1255
00:59:53,620 --> 00:59:55,655
<i>and I might have</i> <i>
to make fire against Mike.</i>

1256
00:59:55,689 --> 00:59:56,931
'Cause the trick is,

1257
00:59:56,965 --> 00:59:59,482
you just want to get
the tiny sticks to ignite

1258
00:59:59,517 --> 01:00:01,482
'cause once you have
those tiny sticks ignited...

1259
01:00:01,517 --> 01:00:02,931
- Yeah.
- ...it's game over.

1260
01:00:03,965 --> 01:00:06,620
<i>
For 21 years,</i> <i>
I've been watching</i> Survivor.

1261
01:00:08,344 --> 01:00:10,413
<i>I always had one dream</i> <i>
in my life.</i>

1262
01:00:10,448 --> 01:00:12,000
The last thing that I would
want to put on the top

1263
01:00:12,034 --> 01:00:15,241
of my résumé of life-- and
I have a pretty good résumé--

1264
01:00:15,275 --> 01:00:16,379
<i>it would be to win</i> Survivor.

1265
01:00:25,000 --> 01:00:28,448
<i>So tonight,</i> <i>
whether I have to make fire</i>

1266
01:00:28,482 --> 01:00:31,517
<i>against Maryanne or Jonathan,</i> <i>
there's only one choice--</i>

1267
01:00:31,551 --> 01:00:33,482
<i>for me to win.</i>

1268
01:00:33,517 --> 01:00:35,793
My fate is in my own hands,

1269
01:00:35,827 --> 01:00:39,724
<i>and I truly feel that if I win</i> <i>
at making fire tonight,</i>

1270
01:00:39,758 --> 01:00:42,724
<i>I will win a million dollars.</i> <i>
So,</i>

1271
01:00:42,758 --> 01:00:44,413
this is for me to lose.

1272
01:01:13,206 --> 01:01:17,827
All right, let's talk
about the past couple of days.

1273
01:01:17,862 --> 01:01:19,827
If you start yesterday morning,
you had a riddle.

1274
01:01:19,862 --> 01:01:21,965
Lindsay solves it.
She gets an advantage

1275
01:01:22,000 --> 01:01:25,241
in the immunity challenge.
Turns out, the time advantage

1276
01:01:25,275 --> 01:01:27,758
was enough, in theory,
to have won.

1277
01:01:27,793 --> 01:01:30,896
But Mike ends up winning,
the guy that some would say,

1278
01:01:30,931 --> 01:01:33,413
least likely to win
on a complicated puzzle.

1279
01:01:33,448 --> 01:01:35,448
- You said it many times.
- Absolutely.

1280
01:01:35,482 --> 01:01:37,034
We get to Tribal Council.

1281
01:01:37,068 --> 01:01:38,724
Lindsay can't persuade you
to keep her

1282
01:01:38,758 --> 01:01:41,448
because she's too big a threat.
She's now on the jury.

1283
01:01:41,482 --> 01:01:45,034
We get to today. Romeo,
a lot of people would have said,

1284
01:01:45,068 --> 01:01:46,482
if you're gonna look
at past history,

1285
01:01:46,517 --> 01:01:48,068
you're the long shot to win.

1286
01:01:48,103 --> 01:01:50,344
And then you win.
And what it reminded me

1287
01:01:50,379 --> 01:01:54,551
is that so much of what
we accomplish in life starts

1288
01:01:54,586 --> 01:01:56,206
with showing up,

1289
01:01:56,241 --> 01:01:59,068
and by showing up,
you're still in the game,

1290
01:01:59,103 --> 01:02:01,793
and you have
all the power tonight.

1291
01:02:01,827 --> 01:02:05,793
So, as you sit here,
what is that feeling of knowing,

1292
01:02:05,827 --> 01:02:08,482
"I hung in there long enough,
and when I needed to,

1293
01:02:08,517 --> 01:02:10,206
I did what I had to do"?

1294
01:02:10,241 --> 01:02:13,172
I mean, I work with all types
of people back home,

1295
01:02:13,206 --> 01:02:16,448
and I encourage them to be
the very best that they can be.

1296
01:02:16,482 --> 01:02:20,689
And somehow, in this game,
for the first time,

1297
01:02:20,724 --> 01:02:24,517
I had to use that advice
that I give them on myself.

1298
01:02:24,551 --> 01:02:28,413
No matter how low I'm feeling,
I still had to keep pushing.

1299
01:02:28,448 --> 01:02:33,206
It's just a reminder that
if you just hang on long enough,

1300
01:02:33,241 --> 01:02:35,068
it can happen.

1301
01:02:35,103 --> 01:02:37,068
And that's why
I was so emotional today

1302
01:02:37,103 --> 01:02:39,655
because I did it,
and I'm very proud of myself.

1303
01:02:39,689 --> 01:02:43,241
All right, before we get
to your decision,

1304
01:02:43,275 --> 01:02:45,068
let me check in
with everybody else. Maryanne,

1305
01:02:45,103 --> 01:02:47,862
- how you feeling?
- You know, you always feel like

1306
01:02:47,896 --> 01:02:49,413
you're going to vomit
'cause it's like,

1307
01:02:49,448 --> 01:02:52,586
I've watched the show and,
like, I've seen people be like,

1308
01:02:52,620 --> 01:02:54,137
yeah, they do fire at camp,
and they get here,

1309
01:02:54,172 --> 01:02:56,413
and they can't do... They can't
even catch a flame, right?

1310
01:02:56,448 --> 01:02:59,586
So, like, even, like, how
confident I feel, it's like

1311
01:02:59,620 --> 01:03:02,379
anything can happen
at Tribal, so...

1312
01:03:02,413 --> 01:03:03,793
Did you practice making fire?

1313
01:03:03,827 --> 01:03:05,275
Yes, I did.

1314
01:03:05,310 --> 01:03:08,103
Jonathan, how are you feeling
about your fire-making skills?

1315
01:03:08,137 --> 01:03:10,517
I'm pretty good at making fires,
Mr. Jeff.

1316
01:03:11,724 --> 01:03:13,482
Mike, what was your take
on the afternoon?

1317
01:03:13,517 --> 01:03:15,896
Well, the worst
kept secret at camp was

1318
01:03:15,931 --> 01:03:18,862
I'm definitely making fire tonight.

1319
01:03:18,896 --> 01:03:21,448
I mean, it's
obviously ironic a bit

1320
01:03:21,482 --> 01:03:22,931
that the fireman
would be making fire,

1321
01:03:22,965 --> 01:03:25,551
but it doesn't mean
you know how to make them

1322
01:03:25,586 --> 01:03:27,551
just because you have
a living of putting them out.

1323
01:03:27,586 --> 01:03:28,793
Very true.

1324
01:03:28,827 --> 01:03:31,586
I watched Jonathan make fire
for the last 12 to 13 days.

1325
01:03:31,620 --> 01:03:32,758
He's very good at it.

1326
01:03:32,793 --> 01:03:34,724
I will give it my best shot.

1327
01:03:34,758 --> 01:03:37,827
So you feel like it's you and
Jonathan. That's what I heard.

1328
01:03:37,862 --> 01:03:39,620
And that's exactly
what I'm saying.

1329
01:03:39,655 --> 01:03:41,758
I feel like it's me and Jonathan.

1330
01:03:41,793 --> 01:03:43,896
They're putting their best
fire maker against me.

1331
01:03:43,931 --> 01:03:45,862
So you're the target?

1332
01:03:47,551 --> 01:03:48,827
Absolutely.

1333
01:03:48,862 --> 01:03:50,137
All right,
well, let's find out.

1334
01:03:50,172 --> 01:03:52,379
So, Romeo, before you tell me,
just walk me through

1335
01:03:52,413 --> 01:03:55,413
the different things
you considered and why.

1336
01:03:55,448 --> 01:03:57,827
Yeah, I mean, I felt
like Miss Universe,

1337
01:03:57,862 --> 01:04:00,172
and this was my crown, and
everybody wanted to talk to me.

1338
01:04:00,206 --> 01:04:01,724
It felt great, uh,

1339
01:04:01,758 --> 01:04:05,034
but it's not as easy
as-as they think it is.

1340
01:04:05,068 --> 01:04:06,793
It was like
a tennis match in my head.

1341
01:04:06,827 --> 01:04:09,034
Am I making the right choice?
I don't know.

1342
01:04:09,068 --> 01:04:11,896
I might be making a million-
dollar mistake, or not.

1343
01:04:11,931 --> 01:04:15,172
I-I don't know, but I've played
my game since day one

1344
01:04:15,206 --> 01:04:18,379
based on my gut feeling,
and I'm still here.

1345
01:04:18,413 --> 01:04:19,931
So obviously
I did something right.

1346
01:04:19,965 --> 01:04:22,103
And, uh, I'm going
with my gut tonight.

1347
01:04:22,137 --> 01:04:24,448
Okay. So, congratulations.

1348
01:04:24,482 --> 01:04:26,896
First spot at the final three
is yours.

1349
01:04:26,931 --> 01:04:28,931
You will get a chance to
plead your case tomorrow night

1350
01:04:28,965 --> 01:04:29,965
to this jury.

1351
01:04:30,000 --> 01:04:31,620
The next decision is

1352
01:04:31,655 --> 01:04:33,413
who's going to be sitting
next to you

1353
01:04:33,448 --> 01:04:36,206
in that second spot
at the final three.

1354
01:04:38,517 --> 01:04:40,586
Who's that gonna be?

1355
01:04:40,620 --> 01:04:41,793
Ah.

1356
01:04:45,448 --> 01:04:47,448
I'm taking Maryanne with me.

1357
01:04:49,206 --> 01:04:50,655
And these two are making fire.

1358
01:04:51,689 --> 01:04:54,034
All right, so, Maryanne,
you are now in the final three.

1359
01:04:54,068 --> 01:04:56,965
You, too, will get a chance to plead your case

1360
01:04:57,000 --> 01:04:58,689
to the jury tomorrow night.

1361
01:04:58,724 --> 01:05:01,344
The only question left
is to see who is going to be

1362
01:05:01,379 --> 01:05:03,793
- the third person next to you.
- I love you, brother.

1363
01:05:03,827 --> 01:05:04,931
I love you, too, man.

1364
01:05:04,965 --> 01:05:05,931
You guys can take your spots.

1365
01:05:05,965 --> 01:05:07,551
Good luck, guys.

1366
01:05:10,758 --> 01:05:13,137
Give you a minute
to look at everything,

1367
01:05:13,172 --> 01:05:14,551
and then we'll begin.

1368
01:05:27,517 --> 01:05:29,689
All right, so,
what you're looking to do

1369
01:05:29,724 --> 01:05:32,103
is make a flame high enough
and hot enough

1370
01:05:32,137 --> 01:05:33,793
to burn through
and raise that flag.

1371
01:05:33,827 --> 01:05:35,241
First to do it will be sitting

1372
01:05:35,275 --> 01:05:36,931
at the final Tribal Council tomorrow.

1373
01:05:36,965 --> 01:05:38,793
The other person will
be sitting on the jury.

1374
01:05:39,827 --> 01:05:41,103
Stakes don't get bigger. No.

1375
01:05:41,137 --> 01:05:43,034
- Are you both ready?
- Yeah.
- Yes.

1376
01:05:43,068 --> 01:05:44,551
Let's begin.

1377
01:05:46,310 --> 01:05:48,965
Been doing this since season 35.

1378
01:05:49,965 --> 01:05:53,827
Both guys get some coconut husk
and start shaving magnesium.

1379
01:05:54,896 --> 01:05:57,344
That magnesium is what's
gonna give you that igniter.

1380
01:06:02,137 --> 01:06:05,000
Jonathan,
now trying to get a spark going.

1381
01:06:08,379 --> 01:06:10,068
It's one thing to do it at camp,

1382
01:06:10,103 --> 01:06:12,310
it's another to do it on
the stage at Tribal Council

1383
01:06:12,344 --> 01:06:15,034
with the million dollars
potentially on the line.

1384
01:06:18,000 --> 01:06:19,275
No flame yet.

1385
01:06:19,310 --> 01:06:21,862
That's pretty normal, too.

1386
01:06:27,689 --> 01:06:29,655
Jonathan going back
for sparks again.

1387
01:06:29,689 --> 01:06:31,620
Had a little something.
Can he get it? No.

1388
01:06:40,000 --> 01:06:42,103
Jonathan once again
trying to nurture

1389
01:06:42,137 --> 01:06:43,206
a little spark into a flame.

1390
01:06:43,241 --> 01:06:44,896
Can't do it.

1391
01:06:44,931 --> 01:06:46,482
Mike still working.

1392
01:06:50,620 --> 01:06:52,310
Mike's got flame first.

1393
01:06:54,724 --> 01:06:56,724
You only have a limited amount
of coconut husk,

1394
01:06:56,758 --> 01:06:58,034
so you don't want
to use all of it.

1395
01:06:58,068 --> 01:06:59,931
It burns quickly,

1396
01:06:59,965 --> 01:07:03,620
but it also burns out
just as fast.

1397
01:07:04,655 --> 01:07:07,896
So once you get a flame,
it's what you do with it.

1398
01:07:09,517 --> 01:07:11,034
Mike going for it.

1399
01:07:11,068 --> 01:07:13,000
He's putting a lot
of coconut husk up there.

1400
01:07:14,517 --> 01:07:15,965
Just dumping sticks on.

1401
01:07:16,000 --> 01:07:17,275
Got to keep it going.

1402
01:07:17,310 --> 01:07:18,965
Jonathan now has
a little something.

1403
01:07:19,000 --> 01:07:21,827
He's working it.
Can he get it to take hold?

1404
01:07:25,000 --> 01:07:27,172
Jonathan's got flame now.

1405
01:07:28,172 --> 01:07:29,172
He's in it.

1406
01:07:29,206 --> 01:07:31,068
He's gonna add
more coconut husk.

1407
01:07:31,103 --> 01:07:33,000
Takes a lot
to burn through that rope.

1408
01:07:34,034 --> 01:07:35,655
The occasional glance
off of the fibers

1409
01:07:35,689 --> 01:07:37,172
of that rope won't be enough.

1410
01:07:37,206 --> 01:07:40,172
You got to get a flame that's
gonna be on there for a moment.

1411
01:07:40,206 --> 01:07:42,310
Mike's is now
starting to hit the rope

1412
01:07:42,344 --> 01:07:44,344
a little more consistently.

1413
01:07:44,379 --> 01:07:46,310
It's shooting pretty high.

1414
01:07:48,482 --> 01:07:49,551
Jonathan has his going.

1415
01:07:49,586 --> 01:07:51,517
Now he's trying
to build something.

1416
01:07:51,551 --> 01:07:52,620
Side by side.

1417
01:07:52,655 --> 01:07:54,862
25 days into <i>Survivor 42.</i>

1418
01:07:54,896 --> 01:07:56,724
A million dollars on the line.

1419
01:07:56,758 --> 01:07:59,068
Mike's flame burning high again.

1420
01:07:59,103 --> 01:08:02,034
You can see that rope burning
little by little.

1421
01:08:03,758 --> 01:08:06,793
Jonathan doing a nice job
to get his fire going.

1422
01:08:06,827 --> 01:08:09,379
We've got two good fires
going right now.

1423
01:08:12,965 --> 01:08:15,275
Mike adding more sticks.

1424
01:08:15,310 --> 01:08:17,241
No real pattern with Mike.

1425
01:08:17,275 --> 01:08:20,000
He's just putting timber
on the flame.

1426
01:08:21,896 --> 01:08:23,896
Jonathan a little more organized,

1427
01:08:23,931 --> 01:08:26,275
trying to build something,
more of a structure.

1428
01:08:27,413 --> 01:08:30,965
Mike is more of a backyard, and
he's burning through that rope.

1429
01:08:33,413 --> 01:08:35,827
Now the wind is
blowing Mike's flame sideways,

1430
01:08:35,862 --> 01:08:37,827
almost into Jonathan.

1431
01:08:37,862 --> 01:08:39,620
You're both still in this,

1432
01:08:39,655 --> 01:08:41,965
but Mike has
a big fire going right now.

1433
01:08:42,000 --> 01:08:44,482
Jonathan has a small fire.

1434
01:08:46,448 --> 01:08:50,068
And Mike's flame
is really starting to burn.

1435
01:08:50,103 --> 01:08:52,517
It is right where you want it.
It is killing it.

1436
01:09:01,482 --> 01:09:04,413
- Yeah! Yes!
- There it is. It's over.

1437
01:09:04,448 --> 01:09:08,413
Yes!
Mike will have the final seat

1438
01:09:08,448 --> 01:09:11,034
at the final Tribal Council
of <i>Survivor 42.</i>

1439
01:09:11,068 --> 01:09:13,103
Oh, my God.
Great matchup.

1440
01:09:13,137 --> 01:09:14,965
Both guys got fire. Boom.

1441
01:09:16,206 --> 01:09:18,034
The fireman pulled it out.

1442
01:09:18,068 --> 01:09:19,034
Mm.

1443
01:09:20,275 --> 01:09:22,413
Jonathan, before you pack up,
have a seat.

1444
01:09:22,448 --> 01:09:24,413
Yeah.

1445
01:09:24,448 --> 01:09:25,724
So what are you thinking,

1446
01:09:25,758 --> 01:09:27,517
Jonathan, when you're
looking at your fire?

1447
01:09:27,551 --> 01:09:28,862
Which is still going.

1448
01:09:28,896 --> 01:09:31,551
That's a decent fire
in the fire-making challenge.

1449
01:09:31,586 --> 01:09:33,655
Mike just built an inferno.

1450
01:09:33,689 --> 01:09:34,724
Yeah.

1451
01:09:35,689 --> 01:09:37,551
Yeah.

1452
01:09:37,586 --> 01:09:39,965
You know what, Jeff?
I was thinking when I got here,

1453
01:09:40,000 --> 01:09:41,793
if-if I lose,
then I was meant to lose.

1454
01:09:41,827 --> 01:09:43,482
I-I gave it what I had.

1455
01:09:44,448 --> 01:09:46,034
Mike's just-- he beat me.

1456
01:09:47,034 --> 01:09:49,000
Yeah, it's that simple.

1457
01:09:49,034 --> 01:09:51,206
Mike, what are you feeling,

1458
01:09:51,241 --> 01:09:53,620
because you're the guy
that just took Jonathan out

1459
01:09:53,655 --> 01:09:55,862
and earned your spot
in the final three?

1460
01:09:55,896 --> 01:09:59,034
You know, it's--
obviously I'm... I-I'm...

1461
01:09:59,068 --> 01:10:01,034
ecstatic over
what just happened.

1462
01:10:01,068 --> 01:10:02,931
Um, I'm happy that
I went against Jonathan,

1463
01:10:02,965 --> 01:10:04,827
because Jonathan
has been known as

1464
01:10:04,862 --> 01:10:06,344
the best fire-starter
in the camp.

1465
01:10:06,379 --> 01:10:08,310
He's been very, very good at it.

1466
01:10:08,344 --> 01:10:12,241
It made it that much more,
um, rewarding for me,

1467
01:10:12,275 --> 01:10:14,000
that I went against somebody
that was...

1468
01:10:14,034 --> 01:10:15,517
not a pushover.

1469
01:10:16,482 --> 01:10:19,655
Jonathan,
you lasted 25 of 26 days.

1470
01:10:19,689 --> 01:10:22,000
You got almost
as far as you can go.

1471
01:10:22,034 --> 01:10:23,551
It's time to grab your torch.

1472
01:10:29,758 --> 01:10:32,482
I love you, brother.
I love you, guys.

1473
01:10:35,758 --> 01:10:37,275
And, Mr. Jeff, I got to say.

1474
01:10:37,310 --> 01:10:38,275
Say it.

1475
01:10:38,310 --> 01:10:40,068
I fought the good fight.

1476
01:10:40,103 --> 01:10:41,758
And, Jonathan...

1477
01:10:41,793 --> 01:10:44,655
The tribe has spoken.

1478
01:10:46,482 --> 01:10:47,517
Time for you to go.

1479
01:10:49,655 --> 01:10:51,689
Hey, my friends.

1480
01:10:53,068 --> 01:10:54,586
All love.
The same.

1481
01:10:54,620 --> 01:10:56,068
Bye, Jon.

1482
01:11:00,655 --> 01:11:04,241
All right,
Mike, Romeo, Maryanne.

1483
01:11:05,034 --> 01:11:06,862
Regardless how you got here,

1484
01:11:06,896 --> 01:11:10,793
you did what 15 other players
in this game could not do.

1485
01:11:10,827 --> 01:11:13,758
You made it to the final three.
Your work is not done.

1486
01:11:13,793 --> 01:11:17,000
Your last job is to
claim your victory,

1487
01:11:17,034 --> 01:11:18,758
and that happens
tomorrow night

1488
01:11:18,793 --> 01:11:21,655
when the power shifts

1489
01:11:21,689 --> 01:11:24,793
to this jury, plus Jonathan,
who will be there tomorrow.

1490
01:11:24,827 --> 01:11:27,482
Tomorrow night they're
gonna put you through a Q and A.

1491
01:11:27,517 --> 01:11:29,896
Their job is to hold you
accountable for your actions

1492
01:11:29,931 --> 01:11:32,206
and make you prove
why you deserve

1493
01:11:32,241 --> 01:11:34,482
the title of Sole Survivor
and the million dollars,

1494
01:11:34,517 --> 01:11:36,482
rather than the other two.

1495
01:11:36,517 --> 01:11:38,862
This is your last night in Fiji.

1496
01:11:38,896 --> 01:11:41,206
I hope you enjoy it.
I hope you get some sleep.

1497
01:11:41,241 --> 01:11:43,793
I'll see you tomorrow night
for your final Tribal Council.

1498
01:11:43,827 --> 01:11:46,000
- Congratulations.
- Thank you so much. Thank you...
- Thanks, Jeff.

1499
01:11:46,965 --> 01:11:49,448
Oh.

1500
01:11:49,482 --> 01:11:52,344
I got to tell you,
I was so shocked

1501
01:11:52,379 --> 01:11:54,241
to see how fast

1502
01:11:54,275 --> 01:11:57,689
my main man Mike
started that fire.

1503
01:11:57,724 --> 01:11:59,758
<i>He beat me fair and square.</i>

1504
01:11:59,793 --> 01:12:03,103
<i>He earned his spot</i> <i>
in the top three.</i>

1505
01:12:03,137 --> 01:12:06,793
<i>And if I get the chance,</i> <i>
you better believe</i>

1506
01:12:06,827 --> 01:12:09,482
<i>that I'm gonna be</i> <i>
right back out here.</i>

1507
01:12:09,517 --> 01:12:12,241
Thank you, God.
Thank you, <i>Survivor.</i>

1508
01:12:12,275 --> 01:12:14,620
Thank you for the opportunity.

1509
01:12:29,034 --> 01:12:30,586
Look at the sun.

1510
01:12:30,620 --> 01:12:32,379
See it right there,
starting to peek through?

1511
01:12:32,413 --> 01:12:34,793
Oh, my God. I love the sun.
Oh, my goodness. That's beautiful.

1512
01:12:34,827 --> 01:12:38,655
It's gonna get warm. It's the 26th day.
Oh, my God.

1513
01:12:38,689 --> 01:12:40,275
There it is.

1514
01:12:40,310 --> 01:12:41,586
Know what's even more beautiful?

1515
01:12:41,620 --> 01:12:43,275
Look how different
all three of us are.

1516
01:12:43,310 --> 01:12:44,482
- And we're still here.
- I know.

1517
01:12:45,517 --> 01:12:48,241
So, it's the morning
of the 26th,

1518
01:12:48,275 --> 01:12:49,758
the last day
you're on <i>Survivor.</i>

1519
01:12:49,793 --> 01:12:53,344
<i>But, of course, I feel</i> <i>
like this game ain't over.</i>

1520
01:12:53,379 --> 01:12:55,241
<i>This game's not over at all.</i>

1521
01:12:55,275 --> 01:12:57,068
<i>And immediately</i> <i>
what goes through my head is:</i>

1522
01:12:57,103 --> 01:12:58,655
what am I gonna say
to the jury?

1523
01:13:01,448 --> 01:13:03,241
How am I gonna talk to the jury?

1524
01:13:03,275 --> 01:13:06,586
<i>Eight jury members are gonna</i> <i>
ask hard-hitting questions.</i>

1525
01:13:07,620 --> 01:13:09,000
I think I'm sitting
in a good spot,

1526
01:13:09,034 --> 01:13:10,172
but does that mean
I'm in a good spot?

1527
01:13:10,206 --> 01:13:11,827
If Mike comes out tonight
and says,

1528
01:13:11,862 --> 01:13:15,310
"My strategy was
to play a man of integrity

1529
01:13:15,344 --> 01:13:17,620
and to stab you in the back,"
fantastic.

1530
01:13:17,655 --> 01:13:20,172
<i>
Mike played a very good game.</i>

1531
01:13:20,206 --> 01:13:22,551
He was able to disarm
and manipulate a lot of people,

1532
01:13:22,586 --> 01:13:26,034
<i>
Mike, using his social game,</i>

1533
01:13:26,068 --> 01:13:27,310
hit the hearts

1534
01:13:27,344 --> 01:13:28,862
<i>of a lot of players.</i>

1535
01:13:28,896 --> 01:13:30,931
<i>
I need Mike to own</i>

1536
01:13:30,965 --> 01:13:32,758
that he was a snake.

1537
01:13:32,793 --> 01:13:35,551
<i>If that was intentional,</i> <i>
he could get my vote</i>

1538
01:13:35,586 --> 01:13:37,034
for a million dollars.

1539
01:13:38,862 --> 01:13:41,068
Oh, my God!
Yes! Yes!

1540
01:13:41,103 --> 01:13:42,275
Oh!

1541
01:13:42,310 --> 01:13:44,965
There's, look, look.
I told you, Danishes.

1542
01:13:45,000 --> 01:13:47,103
Oh, my goodness,
Look at... Give me some, brother.

1543
01:13:47,137 --> 01:13:49,379
Oh, my God!
Yeah.

1544
01:13:49,413 --> 01:13:51,206
If you're voting for the person</i>

1545
01:13:51,241 --> 01:13:52,551
<i>that played the best game,</i>

1546
01:13:52,586 --> 01:13:53,551
give it to me.

1547
01:13:53,586 --> 01:13:55,034
I'm the ultimate underdog.

1548
01:13:55,068 --> 01:13:57,793
Cheers for the most unlikely
final three.

1549
01:13:57,827 --> 01:14:01,034
And one of us winning a million dollars.

1550
01:14:01,068 --> 01:14:04,689
<i>
Now we're going</i> <i>
into the final pageant,</i>

1551
01:14:04,724 --> 01:14:07,551
and I want that crown
and that Miss <i>Survivor</i> sash.

1552
01:14:07,586 --> 01:14:08,758
That's what I want.

1553
01:14:08,793 --> 01:14:11,689
Romeo's strength
was the fact that he was weak.

1554
01:14:11,724 --> 01:14:14,689
<i>He played the game</i> <i>
on a weaker level,</i>

1555
01:14:14,724 --> 01:14:16,137
<i>so he could be forgotten.</i>

1556
01:14:16,172 --> 01:14:18,034
And if that was his strategy
and that's the way he played,

1557
01:14:18,068 --> 01:14:19,241
that's brilliant, dude.

1558
01:14:20,275 --> 01:14:21,896
<i>
Romeo's game might deserve</i>

1559
01:14:21,931 --> 01:14:23,896
<i>a little bit more</i> <i>
credit and respect,</i>

1560
01:14:23,931 --> 01:14:26,827
<i>because basically he said,</i> <i>
"Think of me as a goat."</i>

1561
01:14:26,862 --> 01:14:28,034
Take me to the end,

1562
01:14:28,068 --> 01:14:29,862
and I'm gonna tell you
exactly why I'm not.

1563
01:14:30,896 --> 01:14:33,310
<i>
A lot of us want to reward</i> <i>
the most aggressive player,</i>

1564
01:14:33,344 --> 01:14:37,034
<i>but why is it</i> <i>
more impressive to be</i>

1565
01:14:37,068 --> 01:14:38,758
an elephant than a cockroach,

1566
01:14:38,793 --> 01:14:40,620
who's gonna survive
the apocalypse?

1567
01:14:41,620 --> 01:14:43,068
I'm truly so full right now.

1568
01:14:44,068 --> 01:14:45,068
No. Come on.

1569
01:14:46,517 --> 01:14:47,586
I know.

1570
01:14:47,620 --> 01:14:49,551
<i>To be successful tonight,</i>

1571
01:14:49,586 --> 01:14:52,482
I need to go and be honest
about my game.

1572
01:14:52,517 --> 01:14:53,724
<i>At this point,</i>

1573
01:14:53,758 --> 01:14:55,586
<i>the roller coaster</i> <i>
has already moved.</i>

1574
01:14:55,620 --> 01:14:57,344
<i>There's no getting out,</i>

1575
01:14:57,379 --> 01:14:59,172
<i>which means,</i> <i>
when I go down, I have to</i>

1576
01:14:59,206 --> 01:15:00,551
raise my hands and scream
and be like,

1577
01:15:00,586 --> 01:15:02,965
"This is what I did
in these past 26 days."

1578
01:15:03,000 --> 01:15:06,206
<i>I want to show</i> <i>
that I can still be myself</i>

1579
01:15:06,241 --> 01:15:07,586
<i>and I can still be weird,</i>

1580
01:15:07,620 --> 01:15:09,448
but in the end I can succeed.

1581
01:15:09,482 --> 01:15:12,448
People think she was just used
as a vote, as a pawn,

1582
01:15:12,482 --> 01:15:16,000
<i>which is why I need Maryanne</i> <i>
to articulate what she did</i>

1583
01:15:16,034 --> 01:15:17,896
to drive the season.

1584
01:15:17,931 --> 01:15:20,206
I am so happy for Maryanne.

1585
01:15:20,241 --> 01:15:23,793
<i>She made herself seem</i> <i>
like this silly, younger girl</i>

1586
01:15:23,827 --> 01:15:25,275
<i>who can't be taken seriously,</i>

1587
01:15:25,310 --> 01:15:26,689
but I know there's
a lot more to Maryanne

1588
01:15:26,724 --> 01:15:28,137
than other people are seeing.

1589
01:15:28,172 --> 01:15:29,827
<i>
I was with Maryanne</i> <i>
from day one,</i>

1590
01:15:29,862 --> 01:15:32,344
<i>and yet I have all this unknown.</i>

1591
01:15:32,379 --> 01:15:34,310
<i>You had all this potential</i> <i>
and all this knowledge.</i>

1592
01:15:34,344 --> 01:15:35,655
What did you do with it?

1593
01:15:35,689 --> 01:15:39,344
I hope Maryanne sways me.

1594
01:15:39,379 --> 01:15:40,551
<i>I am a feminist.</i>

1595
01:15:40,586 --> 01:15:42,862
<i>I want to give a woman</i> <i>
some money,</i>

1596
01:15:42,896 --> 01:15:44,344
<i>but I'm also a competitor</i>

1597
01:15:44,379 --> 01:15:46,379
<i>and I can't, in good faith,</i>

1598
01:15:46,413 --> 01:15:48,896
just give someone money
because I like them.

1599
01:15:48,931 --> 01:15:52,241
I did everything
except for win a challenge,

1600
01:15:52,275 --> 01:15:53,793
I believe, on my bucket list.

1601
01:15:56,344 --> 01:15:57,482
And we should be proud,

1602
01:15:57,517 --> 01:15:58,310
'cause we're the last ones
of our tribe.

1603
01:15:58,344 --> 01:15:59,241
Yup.

1604
01:15:59,275 --> 01:16:02,344
One Taku, one Vati, one Ika.

1605
01:16:02,379 --> 01:16:02,931
Yup.

1606
01:16:02,965 --> 01:16:04,034
<i>Don't ever give up.</i>

1607
01:16:04,068 --> 01:16:05,448
<i>You fight and fight and fight.</i>

1608
01:16:05,482 --> 01:16:06,689
This is the final fight.

1609
01:16:06,724 --> 01:16:08,241
You don't, you don't quit
in the fourth quarter.

1610
01:16:08,275 --> 01:16:12,275
I know I can close the deal and
be the winner of <i>Survivor 42.</i>

1611
01:16:12,310 --> 01:16:14,482
<i>
They're about to be</i> <i>
surprised tonight.</i>

1612
01:16:14,517 --> 01:16:18,517
Deep inside this little man,
there's a, uh, a monster.

1613
01:16:18,551 --> 01:16:20,310
We did it, guys. Final three.
We did.

1614
01:16:20,344 --> 01:16:21,620
Good luck tonight, all right? <i>
My vote</i>

1615
01:16:21,655 --> 01:16:23,551
is up for grabs.

1616
01:16:23,586 --> 01:16:26,689
<i>
I'm hoping</i> <i>
somebody comes with some beef</i>

1617
01:16:26,724 --> 01:16:28,034
that deserves
that million dollars.

1618
01:16:28,068 --> 01:16:29,758
<i>
I can only expect</i>

1619
01:16:29,793 --> 01:16:31,758
<i>that the ending of season 42</i>

1620
01:16:31,793 --> 01:16:34,896
will be the most
unpredictable ever.

1621
01:16:38,034 --> 01:16:41,655
<i>
I am making the decision</i> <i>
to change someone's life.</i>

1622
01:16:41,689 --> 01:16:45,103
<i>
What was your move?</i> <i>
How did you drive the game?</i>

1623
01:16:45,137 --> 01:16:46,034
Convince me

1624
01:16:46,068 --> 01:16:48,413
<i>why you deserve my vote.</i>

1625
01:16:48,448 --> 01:16:50,379
Give me straight-up honesty,

1626
01:16:50,413 --> 01:16:52,241
<i>'cause that's</i> <i>
what we're gonna respect.</i>

1627
01:16:52,275 --> 01:16:54,862
And I want them to fight.

1628
01:16:54,896 --> 01:16:56,206
Fight.

1629
01:16:58,068 --> 01:17:00,275
Wow. Here we are.

1630
01:17:00,310 --> 01:17:02,482
Final Tribal Council.

1631
01:17:02,517 --> 01:17:04,758
Romeo, Maryanne, Mike.

1632
01:17:04,793 --> 01:17:07,413
There are stages to <i>Survivor.</i>

1633
01:17:07,448 --> 01:17:10,758
You have the beginning, where
you need to form a strong tribe.

1634
01:17:10,793 --> 01:17:13,586
Then you have
the individual game.

1635
01:17:13,620 --> 01:17:15,068
And then, when
you get down to about five,

1636
01:17:15,103 --> 01:17:16,482
you have that final push,

1637
01:17:16,517 --> 01:17:19,241
and tonight is the last phase:
claim your victory.

1638
01:17:19,275 --> 01:17:20,241
This is it.

1639
01:17:20,275 --> 01:17:22,241
You have to convince

1640
01:17:22,275 --> 01:17:24,137
this group of people
that you voted out--

1641
01:17:24,172 --> 01:17:26,482
you're the reason
they're over there--

1642
01:17:26,517 --> 01:17:28,310
you deserve
the title of Sole Survivor

1643
01:17:28,344 --> 01:17:30,000
and the million dollars
that goes with it.

1644
01:17:30,034 --> 01:17:32,896
If you sit back
and you're passive,

1645
01:17:32,931 --> 01:17:34,551
you will not win this game.

1646
01:17:34,586 --> 01:17:36,586
Juries have shown this repeatedly.

1647
01:17:36,620 --> 01:17:38,517
You got to stand up and take it.

1648
01:17:38,551 --> 01:17:39,827
Demand it.

1649
01:17:39,862 --> 01:17:42,827
Jury, your job is
to hold them accountable.

1650
01:17:42,862 --> 01:17:44,655
Tribal Council has always been

1651
01:17:44,689 --> 01:17:47,655
where you are held accountable
for your actions.

1652
01:17:47,689 --> 01:17:49,793
You're gonna put them
through an interrogation

1653
01:17:49,827 --> 01:17:52,482
that I feel confident
will be tough and respectful.

1654
01:17:52,517 --> 01:17:54,275
Both can exist.

1655
01:17:54,310 --> 01:17:56,103
All right, I'm gonna give

1656
01:17:56,137 --> 01:17:57,379
everybody here a moment.

1657
01:17:59,379 --> 01:18:03,000
One big, deep breath,
and then we'll begin.

1658
01:18:14,965 --> 01:18:16,931
All right, it's time
for our final

1659
01:18:16,965 --> 01:18:19,689
Tribal Council Q and A
from the jury.

1660
01:18:19,724 --> 01:18:21,344
We're gonna examine the game tonight

1661
01:18:21,379 --> 01:18:25,344
from three different areas:
social, physical, strategic.

1662
01:18:25,379 --> 01:18:28,655
And I realize that they often
overlap, and that's okay.

1663
01:18:28,689 --> 01:18:31,103
All right. Who wants
to get us started? Omar.

1664
01:18:31,137 --> 01:18:32,551
All right.

1665
01:18:32,586 --> 01:18:35,068
It's been so long since
we've been able to talk to you,

1666
01:18:35,103 --> 01:18:37,103
so I wanted to congratulate
all three of you.

1667
01:18:37,137 --> 01:18:40,931
And this season
has been so unpredictable.

1668
01:18:40,965 --> 01:18:42,758
And it's so fitting
that you three,

1669
01:18:42,793 --> 01:18:46,172
who may be perceived
as three unexpected players,

1670
01:18:46,206 --> 01:18:48,551
are the ones that made it here.

1671
01:18:48,586 --> 01:18:51,206
And similar to Darwin's theory
of natural selection

1672
01:18:51,241 --> 01:18:52,793
and survival of the fittest,

1673
01:18:52,827 --> 01:18:54,482
it's not always
the mighty elephant

1674
01:18:54,517 --> 01:18:57,310
or the powerful lion
that's gonna win.

1675
01:18:57,344 --> 01:19:00,793
Sometimes it's the honeybee,
which causes prosperity

1676
01:19:00,827 --> 01:19:02,655
in agriculture
across the world,

1677
01:19:02,689 --> 01:19:05,241
or even the cockroach,

1678
01:19:05,275 --> 01:19:07,827
who survives this apocalyptic game...

1679
01:19:07,862 --> 01:19:10,241
that we've had in season 42.

1680
01:19:10,275 --> 01:19:11,896
So, for tonight,

1681
01:19:11,931 --> 01:19:13,586
what we really want you
to do is present

1682
01:19:13,620 --> 01:19:15,827
your survival of the fittest strategy

1683
01:19:15,862 --> 01:19:18,310
and make us sure that
you deserve to win,

1684
01:19:18,344 --> 01:19:21,793
because all our votes
are open tonight for any of you.

1685
01:19:21,827 --> 01:19:24,655
- So fight for your life tonight.
- That's right.

1686
01:19:25,655 --> 01:19:27,620
All right,
let's start with social.

1687
01:19:27,655 --> 01:19:31,241
Okay, so, Mike,
my perception of you,

1688
01:19:31,275 --> 01:19:34,482
from the outside looking in, is
that you're a man of integrity,

1689
01:19:34,517 --> 01:19:36,862
you're a man of honor,
your word means something,

1690
01:19:36,896 --> 01:19:38,862
- you really value a handshake.
- Yeah.

1691
01:19:38,896 --> 01:19:42,931
It appears that you do not want
to lie or deceive in this game.

1692
01:19:42,965 --> 01:19:46,689
Maryanne, my perception of you
is that you're bubbly, young,

1693
01:19:46,724 --> 01:19:49,241
you're talkative,
you're silly and goofy.

1694
01:19:49,275 --> 01:19:50,586
Sometimes you might
take parts of the game

1695
01:19:50,620 --> 01:19:53,896
less seriously than others,
is how it appears.

1696
01:19:53,931 --> 01:19:56,137
And, Romeo,
my perception of you is,

1697
01:19:56,172 --> 01:19:59,206
there are times when
you are quiet, more reserved,

1698
01:19:59,241 --> 01:20:01,793
you know, scattered with bouts
of frantic paranoia

1699
01:20:01,827 --> 01:20:02,793
and random votes at Tribal.

1700
01:20:02,827 --> 01:20:04,379
So my question, to all of you,

1701
01:20:04,413 --> 01:20:07,655
with that perception, is,
is that accurate?

1702
01:20:07,689 --> 01:20:10,275
Is that accurate of how you
played the game, who you are?

1703
01:20:10,310 --> 01:20:12,931
And if not, what am I missing?
Was there more to it?

1704
01:20:12,965 --> 01:20:15,448
- Mike.
- I think it's a great question.

1705
01:20:15,482 --> 01:20:17,551
Um, I think you described me
pretty well.

1706
01:20:17,586 --> 01:20:19,655
Um, I think I've absolutely
played the game

1707
01:20:19,689 --> 01:20:21,482
as honorable
as I could play a game

1708
01:20:21,517 --> 01:20:24,448
that is about deception,
about backstabbing.

1709
01:20:24,482 --> 01:20:26,827
There was only one time
I went against my word,

1710
01:20:26,862 --> 01:20:29,482
and that was to Rocksroy, and
I owe him an apology for that,

1711
01:20:29,517 --> 01:20:31,172
but I think
I've played the game true

1712
01:20:31,206 --> 01:20:33,068
to how I wanted
to play the game.

1713
01:20:33,103 --> 01:20:34,724
Maryanne.

1714
01:20:34,758 --> 01:20:37,241
So, I agree with almost
all of your perception with me.

1715
01:20:37,275 --> 01:20:39,000
The only part
which I don't agree with

1716
01:20:39,034 --> 01:20:41,310
was when you said that I don't
really take the game seriously.

1717
01:20:41,344 --> 01:20:44,137
So, me not taking the game seriously

1718
01:20:44,172 --> 01:20:45,896
was actually
a part of my strategy.

1719
01:20:45,931 --> 01:20:49,103
When I came into the merge, I
realized that there was a trend.

1720
01:20:49,137 --> 01:20:51,689
If you were young,
like under 25, and you seemed

1721
01:20:51,724 --> 01:20:54,034
like you were strategic,
you would be voted out.

1722
01:20:54,068 --> 01:20:57,344
Zach got voted out-- under 25.
Swati got voted out-- under 25.

1723
01:20:57,379 --> 01:20:59,793
Lydia got voted out-- under 25.

1724
01:20:59,827 --> 01:21:01,241
Tori, you were under 25.

1725
01:21:01,275 --> 01:21:02,517
You showed that
you were strategic,

1726
01:21:02,551 --> 01:21:04,586
and you were on the bottom
for the whole time.

1727
01:21:04,620 --> 01:21:07,379
So I basically had to pretend
that I had no strategy,

1728
01:21:07,413 --> 01:21:08,758
and then,
when there were fewer people,

1729
01:21:08,793 --> 01:21:10,758
I'd be able
to start to show my strategy

1730
01:21:10,793 --> 01:21:12,482
further and further in the game.

1731
01:21:13,448 --> 01:21:14,724
Romeo.

1732
01:21:14,758 --> 01:21:16,931
So, the only negative word
that you said about me

1733
01:21:16,965 --> 01:21:18,620
was, uh, "paranoid."

1734
01:21:18,655 --> 01:21:20,482
And, at a certain point, I was,

1735
01:21:20,517 --> 01:21:23,517
because, when we got
to the merge of Kula Kula,

1736
01:21:23,551 --> 01:21:26,413
I quickly went from
feeling like I was the boss

1737
01:21:26,448 --> 01:21:27,862
to the employee.

1738
01:21:27,896 --> 01:21:30,379
And I was at the bottom
of every single Tribal Council.

1739
01:21:30,413 --> 01:21:32,413
And the random votes,

1740
01:21:32,448 --> 01:21:34,413
yes, I did do that,
but that was purposely,

1741
01:21:34,448 --> 01:21:37,206
because I didn't want to vote
for the person that was going.

1742
01:21:37,241 --> 01:21:39,689
Chanelle, I knew you were going.
I didn't vote for you.

1743
01:21:39,724 --> 01:21:42,103
Tori, I'm glad that
I didn't have to vote.

1744
01:21:42,137 --> 01:21:43,965
Hai, you saved me,

1745
01:21:44,000 --> 01:21:45,517
and I told you I wasn't gonna
vote for you when you went,

1746
01:21:45,551 --> 01:21:47,068
and I voted for Jonathan. Um...

1747
01:21:47,103 --> 01:21:50,793
But your strategy of throwing
hinky votes to rile people up,

1748
01:21:50,827 --> 01:21:52,896
you did that to me,
it succeeded,

1749
01:21:52,931 --> 01:21:54,896
and you proceeded
to gaslight me.

1750
01:21:54,931 --> 01:21:57,310
So, was that part
of your social game?

1751
01:21:57,344 --> 01:21:59,034
No, I did not gaslight you.

1752
01:21:59,068 --> 01:22:00,965
You saved me, and
I didn't want to vote for you.

1753
01:22:01,000 --> 01:22:02,586
I refused to vote for you.
Let me, let me specify.

1754
01:22:02,620 --> 01:22:04,137
The gaslighting was
when I asked you

1755
01:22:04,172 --> 01:22:06,551
if you threw the hinky vote
at me at the Chanelle vote-off.

1756
01:22:06,586 --> 01:22:08,034
And you said, "No, I did not."

1757
01:22:08,068 --> 01:22:09,034
Yes.

1758
01:22:09,068 --> 01:22:10,448
So you did gaslight me.

1759
01:22:10,482 --> 01:22:11,827
For that time, yes,

1760
01:22:11,862 --> 01:22:13,103
because you came at me aggressively.

1761
01:22:13,137 --> 01:22:14,724
But you came at me aggressively, too.

1762
01:22:14,758 --> 01:22:17,448
I was just-- I let my feelings
get to me.

1763
01:22:17,482 --> 01:22:18,689
And it-it came from Drea,

1764
01:22:18,724 --> 01:22:20,103
'cause I felt Drea
replaced me with you.

1765
01:22:20,137 --> 01:22:22,413
You were so good
that you... that you were...

1766
01:22:22,448 --> 01:22:23,931
that she replaced me,
and I'm sorry.

1767
01:22:23,965 --> 01:22:25,724
- I'm sorry. I'm sorry.
- Thank you for owning that.

1768
01:22:25,758 --> 01:22:26,862
- Thank you.
- I'm sorry.

1769
01:22:26,896 --> 01:22:28,862
You admitting that
me getting close to Drea

1770
01:22:28,896 --> 01:22:31,068
made you threatened, I respect that.
Yeah. Yeah.

1771
01:22:31,103 --> 01:22:32,586
So thank you for being truthful.

1772
01:22:33,586 --> 01:22:35,413
Anyone else, social?

1773
01:22:35,448 --> 01:22:38,034
Uh, yeah, um, Mike,

1774
01:22:38,068 --> 01:22:40,068
you touted a lot around camp

1775
01:22:40,103 --> 01:22:43,758
about honesty, integrity,
you're a man of your word.

1776
01:22:43,793 --> 01:22:46,448
- Yes.
- And you said earlier, is that the only time

1777
01:22:46,482 --> 01:22:48,344
you've ever lied in the game
was to Rocksroy.

1778
01:22:48,379 --> 01:22:51,862
But did you not lie to Drea
on the beach

1779
01:22:51,896 --> 01:22:54,551
about going after Romeo
to make her feel comfortable?

1780
01:22:54,586 --> 01:22:58,724
And you said, "Omar,
we got to vote out Drea.

1781
01:22:58,758 --> 01:23:01,586
You know I'm just trying to make her comfortable, right?"

1782
01:23:01,620 --> 01:23:03,137
Well, I never purposely

1783
01:23:03,172 --> 01:23:05,689
sacrificed my integrity,
but there were times

1784
01:23:05,724 --> 01:23:08,862
that I had to do things
that maybe I didn't want to do.

1785
01:23:08,896 --> 01:23:10,862
I had to protect myself.

1786
01:23:10,896 --> 01:23:13,517
That's honor for myself, also.

1787
01:23:13,551 --> 01:23:16,413
Mike, I don't think
I hear you owning up

1788
01:23:16,448 --> 01:23:18,310
to what we're asking you. Okay.

1789
01:23:18,344 --> 01:23:19,896
And so, I just want to kind of

1790
01:23:19,931 --> 01:23:21,448
- really dig in.
- Okay.

1791
01:23:21,482 --> 01:23:24,448
How many people in this game
did you shake their hands,

1792
01:23:24,482 --> 01:23:26,827
did you look in their eyes,
did you give your word,

1793
01:23:26,862 --> 01:23:28,586
and then did
you lie to their faces?

1794
01:23:28,620 --> 01:23:29,896
I'm gonna be honest,

1795
01:23:29,931 --> 01:23:32,103
there's only one person
that I shook their hand

1796
01:23:32,137 --> 01:23:34,000
and said something,
and that was Rocksroy.

1797
01:23:34,034 --> 01:23:36,689
Everybody else,
I absolutely kept my word,

1798
01:23:36,724 --> 01:23:40,724
and, until, no, no,
until they deceived me first.

1799
01:23:40,758 --> 01:23:42,034
And I'll explain what happened.

1800
01:23:42,068 --> 01:23:44,206
Rocksroy says to me,
I say to him,

1801
01:23:44,241 --> 01:23:46,206
"Is this easy as it is?"
We shook hands.

1802
01:23:46,241 --> 01:23:47,517
I said, "I'm voting Romeo."

1803
01:23:47,551 --> 01:23:49,172
At the last minute,
you came up to me and said,

1804
01:23:49,206 --> 01:23:51,000
"Listen, we have
to vote Rocksroy off."

1805
01:23:51,034 --> 01:23:52,172
I said,
"I can't vote Rocksroy off.

1806
01:23:52,206 --> 01:23:53,586
I just told him
I wasn't voting him off."

1807
01:23:53,620 --> 01:23:55,068
And you said, "No, we have to."

1808
01:23:55,103 --> 01:23:57,068
I said, "If we're in an alliance
and I'm your number one,

1809
01:23:57,103 --> 01:23:59,655
"how come I didn't know
until 30 minutes prior

1810
01:23:59,689 --> 01:24:00,896
to us going to a Tribal?"

1811
01:24:00,931 --> 01:24:02,827
You shook my hand,
and you blindsided me.

1812
01:24:02,862 --> 01:24:04,793
I was never deceitful. Your words are...
Yes, but then, okay.

1813
01:24:04,827 --> 01:24:07,068
So you're telling me
that you weren't deceitful?

1814
01:24:07,103 --> 01:24:09,310
- Then-then I...
- I think somebody else might have lied to you.

1815
01:24:09,344 --> 01:24:12,034
You don't realize that Omar was
lying to you the entire time?

1816
01:24:12,068 --> 01:24:14,137
But then you weren't talking to me.
Yes, I was, Mike.

1817
01:24:14,172 --> 01:24:16,034
I didn't even know you were
in an alliance with them.

1818
01:24:16,068 --> 01:24:17,379
I told you.

1819
01:24:17,413 --> 01:24:19,379
It kind of comes down to,
anybody who's aligned with you

1820
01:24:19,413 --> 01:24:21,551
is not allowed
to talk to other people...

1821
01:24:21,586 --> 01:24:24,275
- Mm.
- ...when that's how people get information

1822
01:24:24,310 --> 01:24:26,827
to be able to give you,
yet you are allowed

1823
01:24:26,862 --> 01:24:29,206
to talk to lots of different
people and have one-on-ones.

1824
01:24:29,241 --> 01:24:31,517
And that's where
it seems inconsistent.

1825
01:24:31,551 --> 01:24:33,275
That's true.
But was that the strategy?

1826
01:24:33,310 --> 01:24:34,655
We're trying to understand,
was that strategy,

1827
01:24:34,689 --> 01:24:35,689
or was that just like...?
It was.

1828
01:24:35,724 --> 01:24:37,172
It was absolutely strategy
to use

1829
01:24:37,206 --> 01:24:39,172
my social game for the alliance
I was in and for myself

1830
01:24:39,206 --> 01:24:41,068
to advance in the game.
Okay, but you just claimed

1831
01:24:41,103 --> 01:24:45,344
that your game was to be honest
and have dignity.

1832
01:24:45,379 --> 01:24:48,034
That is not what
it's sounding like, Mike.

1833
01:24:48,068 --> 01:24:50,206
- You need to own your game.
- Well... I am, I'm saying it right now.

1834
01:24:50,241 --> 01:24:52,034
I just want to,
I just want us to settle down

1835
01:24:52,068 --> 01:24:53,379
because we all lied to people.

1836
01:24:53,413 --> 01:24:58,206
Mike, I actually think
your social game was on point.

1837
01:24:58,241 --> 01:25:00,896
You were very social
with everyone.

1838
01:25:00,931 --> 01:25:03,482
And kudos to you,
as a 57-year-old,

1839
01:25:03,517 --> 01:25:06,034
staying in the talks
with all of us--

1840
01:25:06,068 --> 01:25:07,862
people who are half your age
most of the time.

1841
01:25:07,896 --> 01:25:11,344
Thank you. Fortunately my social
game is what I am in real life.

1842
01:25:11,379 --> 01:25:13,586
I'm a very social person.
I like people.

1843
01:25:13,620 --> 01:25:14,758
I want to know
what makes them tick.

1844
01:25:14,793 --> 01:25:16,896
And you guys
opened up your world to me,

1845
01:25:16,931 --> 01:25:18,551
introducing me to places, cultures,

1846
01:25:18,586 --> 01:25:21,206
religions that I never knew
before, and I just ate it up.

1847
01:25:21,241 --> 01:25:24,068
So when I talk to people,
people like me,

1848
01:25:24,103 --> 01:25:26,827
and they would just come up
to me and give me information.

1849
01:25:26,862 --> 01:25:29,206
I-I respect that,
'cause your social game

1850
01:25:29,241 --> 01:25:30,724
is the reason I went home,
straight up.

1851
01:25:30,758 --> 01:25:32,241
Like, it saved you.

1852
01:25:32,275 --> 01:25:33,551
Thank you.

1853
01:25:33,586 --> 01:25:35,655
- I have a question for you, Maryanne.
- Mm-hmm.

1854
01:25:35,689 --> 01:25:38,517
At Taku,
I felt that your social game

1855
01:25:38,551 --> 01:25:41,241
put you on the bottom.

1856
01:25:41,275 --> 01:25:45,413
Did you realize
that your sloppy social game

1857
01:25:45,448 --> 01:25:46,862
was putting you in danger,

1858
01:25:46,896 --> 01:25:50,172
and did you do anything to
change that later in the game?

1859
01:25:50,206 --> 01:25:52,103
Yep. And I can understand that,

1860

The person who I feel

1991

and my best move was

2053

2087

2088

2090

that I work with,

2091

I didn't give up.

2092

I didn't give up.

682
00:31:45,586 --> 00:31:49,275
Last time you can vote somebody
out of this game, Jesse.

683
00:31:49,379 --> 00:31:52,137
You survive tonight,
your fate is in your hands.

684
00:31:52,241 --> 00:31:54,448
You either win at final four,
somebody takes you

685
00:31:54,551 --> 00:31:56,827

or you get to make fire.

686
00:31:56,931 --> 00:31:59,896
How does that shift the level
of threat management

687
00:32:00,000 --> 00:32:01,862
that has to happen

688
00:32:01,965 --> 00:32:05,103
if you think you're the one
that everybody's worried about?

689
00:32:05,206 --> 00:32:07,137
Uh, you just start
trying to play up

690
00:32:07,241 --> 00:32:09,068

691
00:32:09,172 --> 00:32:11,413
You start trying to push them
in front of the bus.

692
00:32:11,517 --> 00:32:14,620
I had, uh, you know, someone
earlier today try and push me

693
00:32:14,724 --> 00:32:17,103
in front of the bus and play
at my threat level and...

694
00:32:17,206 --> 00:32:18,551
You looked directly at Karla.

695
00:32:18,655 --> 00:32:20,000
Yeah, Karla has, uh,

696
00:32:20,103 --> 00:32:22,034
been throwing punches today, so...

697

Well, last Tribal, someone

698
00:32:24,724 --> 00:32:28,379

and then washed another idol

699

to save someone, right?

700
00:32:30,758 --> 00:32:32,931
And I was like, "Dang."

701
00:32:33,034 --> 00:32:37,000
That is one of the best moves
I've ever seen on <i>Survivor.</i>

702
00:32:37,103 --> 00:32:38,344
We're talking about Jesse.

703
00:32:38,448 --> 00:32:39,655
And we're talking exactly
about Jessie.

704
00:32:39,758 --> 00:32:41,586
And, you know, the jury sees

705
00:32:41,689 --> 00:32:43,896
the one person
who takes the idol and says

706
00:32:44,000 --> 00:32:46,206

707
00:32:46,310 --> 00:32:48,137
That is the memory
that's engraved

708
00:32:48,241 --> 00:32:51,000

of who made that move.

709
00:32:51,103 --> 00:32:52,862
So you're saying,
"Jesse made a big move.

710
00:32:52,965 --> 00:32:56,310
That's why it should be Jesse
that we take out"?

711
00:32:56,413 --> 00:32:57,896
Exactly.

712
00:32:58,000 --> 00:33:00,137
So, Jesse, from your standpoint,

713
00:33:00,241 --> 00:33:02,310

what do you do?

714
00:33:03,344 --> 00:33:05,172
I feel good tonight.
Like, I feel good.

715
00:33:05,275 --> 00:33:09,413
I mean, Owen's safe,
and I know I'm safe

716
00:33:09,517 --> 00:33:11,931
because I've been hanging
onto this little thing

717
00:33:12,034 --> 00:33:13,482

718
00:33:13,586 --> 00:33:16,793
And, uh, so...

719
00:33:22,206 --> 00:33:24,068
I-I'm punching my ticket
to the final four tonight,

720
00:33:24,172 --> 00:33:25,931
so either way...

721
00:33:29,896 --> 00:33:32,793
I mean, I'm good.
You know, I'm good. I'm fine.

722
00:33:32,896 --> 00:33:36,448
Cassidy, your jaw was open

723
00:33:36,551 --> 00:33:38,068
- for that entire time.
- Yeah.

724
00:33:38,172 --> 00:33:39,965
I think that was Jeanine's idol,
maybe, in his pocket.

725
00:33:40,068 --> 00:33:42,034
So I guess
Dwight pulled a switcheroo

726
00:33:42,137 --> 00:33:45,310
and maybe gave Jeanine's idol
to him.

727
00:33:45,413 --> 00:33:46,620
It looks pretty familiar to me.
I mean,

728
00:33:46,724 --> 00:33:48,724
that looks like the bead
that Jeanine got off

729
00:33:48,827 --> 00:33:51,241
my bag back at Baka way back.

730
00:33:51,344 --> 00:33:53,793
So, I-I was also under
the impression that it went home

731
00:33:53,896 --> 00:33:56,241

00:33:56,344 --> 00:33:57,965
my jaw dropped

733
00:34:00,206 --> 00:34:03,827
Karla, does it
make you nervous now that

Jesse has dangled
what he says is an idol?

735
00:34:05,862 --> 00:34:09,275
Owen says, "I recognize a bead,"

736
00:34:09,379 --> 00:34:11,827
Yeah, I mean, it's...

737
00:34:11,931 --> 00:34:15,137
It was a flex.
He has an idol, if it's real.

738
00:34:15,241 --> 00:34:16,482
So, at this point,
if anyone wants

739
00:34:16,586 --> 00:34:18,000
to make any other move, I mean,

740
00:34:18,103 --> 00:34:20,000
there are two other options.

741
00:34:20,103 --> 00:34:22,206
Cassidy, she's basically talking

742
00:34:22,310 --> 00:34:23,862
- you or Gabler.
- Yeah. No, of course.

743
00:34:23,965 --> 00:34:25,379
I could see her kind of driving
any pitch at this point.

744
00:34:25,482 --> 00:34:26,931
That's how good
of a player she is,

745
00:34:27,034 --> 00:34:28,482
you know, and-and that's
the reason that

746
00:34:28,586 --> 00:34:31,068
she's being targeted tonight, as
much as she's trying to downplay

747
00:34:31,172 --> 00:34:33,793
- her threat level.
- I don't know.
Like, honestly,

748
00:34:33,896 --> 00:34:35,068
maybe it's because
I'm being honest.

749
00:34:35,172 --> 00:34:36,448
Maybe it's because
they're like, "Let's just

750
00:34:36,551 --> 00:34:38,551

and send her to the jury."

751
00:34:38,655 --> 00:34:41,275
But they think I'm a threat?

752
00:34:41,379 --> 00:34:44,344
I mean, you have threats
in front of you.

753
00:34:44,448 --> 00:34:47,655
If people want to make bigger
moves-- and I don't know if

754
00:34:47,758 --> 00:34:50,758

doing an even bigger move--

755
00:34:50,862 --> 00:34:52,896
I mean, the floor
is open, right?

756
00:34:53,000 --> 00:34:55,034
- Let's do it.
- Yeah, I mean, so,

757
00:34:55,137 --> 00:34:57,344
I've been thinking
about this all day, you know?

758
00:34:57,448 --> 00:34:58,689
I definitely will
entertain more ideas

759
00:34:58,793 --> 00:35:01,724
if you have 'em, so...

760
00:35:01,827 --> 00:35:03,275
Would you like to dance, sir?

761
00:35:03,379 --> 00:35:05,482
- We can dance.
- Let's dance.

762
00:35:24,689 --> 00:35:26,137
Um...

763
00:35:29,620 --> 00:35:31,103
- Jesse, can we talk to you?
- Yeah.
- The two of you?

764
00:35:31,206 --> 00:35:32,344
- Come over here?
- Yeah.

765
00:35:32,448 --> 00:35:33,689
- Just the two of us.
- Okay, cool.

766
00:35:33,793 --> 00:35:35,827
So, Owen, how you feeling

767
00:35:35,931 --> 00:35:37,586
- right now?
- Freaking the heck out.

768
00:35:37,689 --> 00:35:38,896
- Like, just thinking about...
- For real?

769
00:35:39,000 --> 00:35:40,896
Yeah, for real.
I mean, we have...

770
00:35:41,000 --> 00:35:43,379
This has been
a very subtle season,

771
00:35:43,482 --> 00:35:47,172
and to have it finally boil over
like this is just...

772
00:35:47,275 --> 00:35:48,448
it's wild.

773
00:35:51,172 --> 00:35:52,655
This is a lot, Jeff.

774
00:36:09,034 --> 00:36:11,241
- Okay.
- Wow.
And just like that,

775
00:36:11,344 --> 00:36:13,172
everybody sat back down together.

776
00:36:13,275 --> 00:36:14,931
- How are you feeling, Cassidy?
- I mean, I'm definitely

777
00:36:15,034 --> 00:36:17,068
more nervous
than when I started the night.

778
00:36:17,172 --> 00:36:20,103
You know, Karla's been trying
to talk up like

779
00:36:20,206 --> 00:36:22,448
she's less of a threat than me
and... and yada, yada, yada.

780
00:36:22,551 --> 00:36:23,724
She's been pretty much
saying that

781
00:36:23,827 --> 00:36:25,103
about everybody
and everything, and...

782
00:36:25,206 --> 00:36:26,724
But, you know,
I think me and Jesse also have

783
00:36:26,827 --> 00:36:28,068
a really good relationship,

784
00:36:28,172 --> 00:36:29,448
and we've worked together
on many votes,

785
00:36:29,551 --> 00:36:31,379
and including this last vote.

786
00:36:31,482 --> 00:36:32,724
And so, you know,
I mean, I hope that

787
00:36:32,827 --> 00:36:34,379
that holds some sway to him.

788
00:36:34,482 --> 00:36:35,724
Gabler, how about you?

789
00:36:35,827 --> 00:36:38,172
You know, the-the turmoil

790
00:36:38,275 --> 00:36:41,758
and the chaos that's been
going on all day today?

791
00:36:41,862 --> 00:36:44,103
Everyone has been
vehemently targeted

792

with a great plan,
and then, like,

793
00:36:46,448 --> 00:36:48,310
literally, when you turn away,
somebody else walks up.

794
00:36:48,413 --> 00:36:50,448
There's another one, and
it's-it's for the next person,

795
00:36:50,551 --> 00:36:52,655
the next person.
It's anybody.

796
00:36:56,965 --> 00:37:00,206
And on that note,
it is time to vote. Gabler,

797
00:37:00,310 --> 00:37:02,758
- you're up.
- Gotcha.

798
00:37:14,827 --> 00:37:16,241
I liked you in this game,

799
00:37:16,344 --> 00:37:18,448

on my résumé.

800
00:37:35,655 --> 00:37:37,172
If anybody has
an advantage or an idol

801

now would be the time to do so.

802
00:37:41,000 --> 00:37:42,862
I don't think I need it,

803
00:37:42,965 --> 00:37:45,758
um, but my good friend Cody

804
00:37:45,862 --> 00:37:48,931

take the guarantee.

805
00:37:49,034 --> 00:37:51,827
- So I'm playing the idol
on myself.
- Got it.

806
00:37:54,206 --> 00:37:56,310
This is a hidden immunity idol.

807
00:37:56,413 --> 00:37:59,034
Any votes cast for Jesse
will not count.

808
00:37:59,137 --> 00:38:01,965
All right, I'll read the votes.

809
00:38:06,103 --> 00:38:08,172
First vote: Jesse.

810
00:38:08,275 --> 00:38:10,034
Does not count.

811
00:38:11,689 --> 00:38:14,724
Karla. One vote Karla.

812
00:38:18,862 --> 00:38:22,448
- Karla.
That's two votes Karla.
- Oh, yes.

813
00:38:27,103 --> 00:38:30,586
Fourteenth person voted out
of <i>Survivor</i> 43: Karla.

814
00:38:30,689 --> 00:38:31,896
That's three. That's enough.

815
00:38:32,000 --> 00:38:33,172
And that's how
you play a game, you guys.

816
00:38:33,275 --> 00:38:34,517
You're a rock star.
You're a rock star.

817
00:38:34,620 --> 00:38:36,206
- Good game, Karla.
- Thank you.

818
00:38:36,310 --> 00:38:38,413
That was amazing, man.

819
00:38:50,241 --> 00:38:52,413
Oh, man!

820
00:38:52,517 --> 00:38:56,275
This feels so good, Jeff.

821
00:38:58,689 --> 00:38:59,896
- Karla?
- Yes.

822
00:39:00,000 --> 00:39:02,068
The tribe has spoken.

823
00:39:03,551 --> 00:39:05,310
- Good luck, y'all.
- Have a great night.

824
00:39:05,413 --> 00:39:07,103
- I love y'all.
- Bye, Karla.

825
00:39:15,793 --> 00:39:18,482
Well, you have made it
to the final four.

826
00:39:18,586 --> 00:39:22,344
Tomorrow, you will compete in
your final immunity challenge.

827
00:39:22,448 --> 00:39:23,793
Try to get some sleep.

828
00:39:23,896 --> 00:39:26,379
Grab your torches.
Head back to camp. Good night.

829
00:39:26,482 --> 00:39:28,068
Good night, Jeff.

830
00:39:29,448 --> 00:39:31,068
I think I played
a kick-ass game

831
00:39:31,172 --> 00:39:33,758
<i>and to hear people think</i>

832
00:39:33,862 --> 00:39:35,896
<i>that I was a great threat,
a great player,</i>

833
00:39:36,000 --> 00:39:38,689
<i>that is the highest honor,
I think, in this game.</i>

834
00:39:38,793 --> 00:39:41,344
There's no other way
I would have wanted to go.

835
00:39:50,275 --> 00:39:51,551
If you think you have what
it takes to live in a jungle,

836
00:39:51,655 --> 00:39:52,931
compete in challenges

837
00:39:53,034 --> 00:39:54,724
and vote each other out,
apply to be on <i>Survivor.</i>

838
00:40:12,655 --> 00:40:14,896
Come on in.

839
00:40:27,000 --> 00:40:30,793
Welcome to day 25...

840
00:40:30,896 --> 00:40:33,758
and your final
immunity channel.

841
00:40:41,068 --> 00:40:44,413
All right.
Shall we get to your final

842
00:40:44,517 --> 00:40:45,827
immunity challenge?

843
00:40:45,931 --> 00:40:47,206
- Yes, sir.
- Yes, sir.
- Yes.

844
00:40:47,310 --> 00:40:49,137
One more time.
Owen, got to take back

845
00:40:49,241 --> 00:40:50,586
- the necklace.
- All right.

846
00:40:51,655 --> 00:40:53,724
- Thank you.
- Thank you.

847
00:40:57,275 --> 00:41:00,827
Once again,
and for the last time,

848
00:41:00,931 --> 00:41:03,827
immunity is back up for grabs.

849
00:41:03,931 --> 00:41:06,620
For today's challenge,
you're gonna use a long fork

850
00:41:06,724 --> 00:41:09,206
<i>to maneuver a bowl
through a channel.</i>

851
00:41:09,310 --> 00:41:11,655
<i>When you get to the top,</i>

852
00:41:11,758 --> 00:41:14,413
<i>you'll place your bowl,
head back for the next one.</i>

853
00:41:14,517 --> 00:41:16,172
<i>What makes it tricky
is the entire structure</i>

854
00:41:16,275 --> 00:41:19,275
<i>sits on a spring, which means
if you hit the structure</i>

855
00:41:19,379 --> 00:41:23,586
<i>too hard, it will wobble,
your bowls will drop,</i>

856
00:41:23,689 --> 00:41:25,241
<i>you got to start again.</i>

857
00:41:25,344 --> 00:41:29,000
<i>First person
to stack 15 bowls...</i>

858
00:41:30,206 --> 00:41:31,724

859
00:41:31,827 --> 00:41:33,241

in the final three,

860
00:41:33,344 --> 00:41:34,931

get a chance to plead

861
00:41:35,034 --> 00:41:39,241

about why you deserve the title

862
00:41:39,344 --> 00:41:41,724
